# R0020: Make default real-time mode follow device wall-clock corrections

**Repository-local identity:** `R0020` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#32](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/32). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Campaign draft alias: SW-032. Existing corrective owner: GitHub #32. Proposed priority P1; product-or-skill defect. The main repair target is `fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624`; audit `9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb` is comparison evidence, not an assumed future target. This work order authorizes no implementation, commit or publication.

## Captured divergence and the missing clock authority

The widget has one public temporal source, but ordinary mode does not keep that source aligned with the device wall clock. `initSim()` records Date.now once. `simNow()` then adds only monotonic elapsed time until the timezone changes. NEW-HP-001's exact-source fixture moved Date.now and performance.now independently: unchanged clocks had zero skew; a +3600000 ms wall correction left `simNow-Date.now=-3600000`; a −3600000 correction left +3600000. ET-NEW-001 corroborated the same defect with ±7200000 ms plus one second of monotonic elapsed time. These are two witnesses of one invariant, not two clock owners.

The old formula is arithmetically consistent with its old anchor. Its defect is using that retained anchor as ordinary **current device time** after the device has corrected itself. Prayer/current-event selection, countdown, civil day, sun/moon date and day acquisition consume this instant; changing only a text clock would leave the product state wrong. There is no evidence here of an actual NTP incident, an observed user's error duration, a measured correction frequency, a native suspend result, or a rendered/public repair. Historical results used exact temporal source in controlled Node environments and did not change the machine clock.

DST elapsed arithmetic remains [R0007](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/7), conversion of explicit local times remains [R0008](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/8), and day/late-response/Hijri semantics remain their existing owners. This issue supplies the correct current instant and discriminating consumer cases.

## Re-anchor and resolve explicit timeScale=1 from the actual contract

Before edits, record `git -C C:\workspace\ai\salah_widget rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `rev-parse HEAD`, `status --short`, and `diff -- index.html DESIGN.md tests/smoke.html`, with the same `git -C` prefix. Compare [main initialization/mode helpers](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L694-L726), [loop and visibility](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L2224-L2273), and [candidate temporal source](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/index.html#L709-L744). Stop on incompatible relevant drift; unrelated work remains untouched.

The existing code distinguishes an absent `timeScale` parameter from an explicit positive one: `ADVANCING = _tsParam!=null && TIMESCALE>0`. Explicit `timeScale=1` therefore already selects preview behavior: [hourly forecast synchronization](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L861-L866), [star reprojection](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L1983-L1985), [SIM readout](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L2032-L2034), and the loop's forecast/refresh/fast-class branches. [DESIGN's parameter contract](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/DESIGN.md#L246-L250) expressly says a timeScale parameter enables ADVANCING, forecast weather, reprojected stars and the sim clock.

There is a conflicting shorthand comment: “1 → real time.” In context that states the **rate**, while the executable parameter-presence branch and documented preview effects distinguish mode intent. The chosen minimal repair preserves explicit `timeScale=1` as a 1× anchored preview. It fixes only ordinary no-clock-override loads. This is an evidence-based compatibility choice, not an assertion that the old wording was unambiguous. Clarify the comment and DESIGN: absent clock overrides follows current device time; explicit `timeScale=1` remains a 1× preview with its existing preview behavior. Do not use this issue to change ADVANCING/weather semantics or silently reinterpret existing preview URLs.

## Exact mode table and smallest source design

Define the authority predicate once, beside existing parsed flags. Proposed code below is design, not an implemented patch:

```js
const FOLLOW_WALL_CLOCK =
  _tsParam == null && SIM.time == null && TIMESCALE === 1;

function simNow(){
  if(FOLLOW_WALL_CLOCK) return Date.now();
  if(_simBase == null || _simTz !== tz) initSim();
  return _simBase + (_RAFNOW()-_rafT0)*TIMESCALE;
}
```

Integrate the converter owner's explicit invalid-simulation guard around the explicit branch; do not reintroduce a numeric old anchor after a rejected scene. The predicate has no persisted state and no new query field. It deliberately distinguishes parameter presence from the numeric rate.

| Inputs after existing parsing | Clock authority | Existing visible/data mode retained |
|---|---|---|
| No simTime, no timeScale | Current Date.now on every call | Ordinary real-time; no new ADVANCING flag. |
| Explicit timeScale=1, no simTime | Initial anchor plus monotonic elapsed ×1 | Existing 1× preview/ADVANCING and SIM readout. |
| Explicit timeScale=60, no simTime | Initial anchor plus monotonic elapsed ×60 | Existing accelerated preview. |
| simTime=03:30, no timeScale | Resolved explicit anchor, scale 0 | Frozen scene remains frozen. |
| simTime=03:30 with scale 1 or 60 | Resolved anchor plus configured elapsed rate | Explicit scene remains independent. |
| Explicit scale 0, empty/invalid scale parsed as 0, or clamped negative scale | Existing frozen parsed mode | Do not broaden this task into query-parser validation. |

1. Put the ordinary branch before any retained-anchor initialization. A zone change changes how an epoch is displayed, not the real epoch itself; ordinary mode need not call `initSim` merely because `_simTz` is stale. Leave explicit simulation's intended zone-settling initialization in place. Do not repeatedly reanchor its elapsed base every frame.
2. Keep `nowParts()` and `simDate()` on the same `simNow()` entry point. Do not add separate “real date,” “prayer clock” and “sky clock” authorities or call Date.now directly throughout the renderer. A current default-mode call must observe either direction of a wall step immediately. The existing `sec!==_lastSec` loop comparison schedules rendering after either positive or negative second changes; preserve `!==`, not `>`.
3. Make consumer decisions with the ordinary current instant on their next existing scheduled render. [R0007](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/7) owns a coherent model snapshot for endpoint subtraction. There is no requirement to introduce a global frame cache or another rAF loop here. A subsecond correction within the same integer second can be shown at the next normal second tick; the fixture must not claim a callback occurred when the loop was paused.
4. On forward/backward civil-day corrections, preserve the day-adoption contract from [R0005](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/5): derive the actual current local day, classify completed cache/prefetch and late data by their admitted dates, and mark an unmatched retained record stale/unavailable. Do not increment the configuration generation on every clock read. A same-generation pending response can still have the wrong day after a correction, so [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3) generation guards are necessary but not sufficient.
5. The candidate's future-Hijri hold is not automatically adopted into main. If the final integrated date-output owner uses a hold, [R0009](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/9) must disclose it correctly after a backward step rather than silently calling a future date current. The clock repair must not hide its restored ability to move backward behind a monotonic display clamp. Shared consumer evidence may qualify both owners without moving their source ownership here.
6. Preserve real-elapsed operation eligibility and busy ownership under [R0006](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/6). A wall correction should change the relevant civil day, not cause one request per frame or postpone an otherwise eligible retry by an hour. `_RAFNOW()` uses performance.now on the normal supported browser path; where its existing fallback is Date.now, independent-simulation/monotonic guarantees require actual host qualification and are not inferred from Node stubs.
7. Retain the existing visibility and IntersectionObserver stop/start behavior. A hidden document does not need a timer to keep updating output; its first resumed callback reads the current wall instant and performs at most the existing eligible day/acquisition work. Do not run a catch-up render or request for every missed second/day. Actual native sleep/wake is a separate environment pathway and cannot be declared fixed from injected clock steps alone.

Periodic blind reanchors would destroy frozen/accelerated scenes. A new “NTP detector” or correction threshold invents policy not needed by the witness. Keeping only monotonic time preserves the defect indefinitely. Changing ADVANCING to hide the explicit-1 difference would alter forecast/stars/UI behavior outside scope. Direct Date.now for the default branch is smaller and exact for the specified authority.

## Public deterministic RED → GREEN fixture

The following **proposed** fixture controls only its VM Date/performance objects. It does not alter the host clock or execute a private probe. It extracts the actual temporal block; preserve its source hash and stop if markers are missing. Each test creates a fresh realm so one mode's anchor cannot contaminate another.

```js
const fs = require('node:fs'), vm = require('node:vm');
const assert = require('node:assert/strict');
const source = fs.readFileSync('index.html','utf8');
const a = source.indexOf('const _RAFNOW =');
const b = source.indexOf('// ---- prayer-times data:',a);
assert(a >= 0 && b > a);
const block = source.slice(a,b);
const base = Date.parse('2026-09-07T12:00:00.000Z');
function check(query, step, expected){
  let wall=base, mono=0;
  class ClockDate extends Date {
    constructor(...args){ super(...(args.length ? args : [wall])); }
    static now(){ return wall; }
  }
  const q=new URLSearchParams(query);
  const c=vm.createContext({Date:ClockDate, Intl, q,
    SIM:{time:q.get('simTime')}, tz:'UTC',
    performance:{now:()=>mono}, pad:n=>String(n).padStart(2,'0')});
  vm.runInContext(block,c);
  const read=()=>vm.runInContext('simNow()',c,{timeout:5000});
  read(); // establish the explicit-mode anchor before either clock changes
  mono=1000; wall=base+1000+step;
  assert.equal(read(), expected(wall));
}
for(const step of [0,3600000,-3600000,7200000,-7200000])
  check('',step,wall=>wall);
check('timeScale=1',3600000,()=>base+1000);
check('timeScale=60',3600000,()=>base+60000);
check('simTime=03:30',3600000,
      ()=>Date.parse('2026-09-07T03:30:00.000Z'));
```

The default positive/negative assertions fail on the historical source by exactly the injected step; unchanged clock is the positive control. The explicit-preview assertions preserve its existing independent anchor/rate. The timeout is fixture containment, not a production clock deadline. Repeat negative wall steps for explicit modes and SIM.time+scale; each must remain independent on the supplied monotonic performance fixture. Also assert default `nowParts()` is 13:00:01 or 11:00:01 UTC after the respective one-hour step, proving that wall parts consume the corrected instant.

## Required caller and browser controls

An isolated browser fixture must inject its test Date/performance functions **before** the widget script executes, then supply deterministic provider responses and storage. Use a same-origin disposable document or test runner's pre-script hook; changing a `window.Date` object after the IIFE has already captured state is not equivalent setup. Record the served source hash and actual hook installation, invoke the real boot/render/loop, and capture DOM output. A detached Node function test does not prove browser consumer integration.

Use a synthetic admitted UTC September 7 record with Fajr 05:00, Sunrise 06:00, Dhuhr 12:00, Asr 15:30, Maghrib/Sunset 18:00, Isha 19:30, matching Gregorian fields and UTC metadata. These are fixture inputs, not a real site's prayer prediction.

| Controlled transition | Required actual consumer result |
|---|---|
| 15:29:59 → 15:30:01 wall step, fixed monotonic time | Next scheduled visible render changes current prayer from Dhuhr to Asr; next key becomes Maghrib, and countdown consumes the new instant. |
| Reverse to 15:29:59 | Current/next selection can return to Dhuhr/Asr; no only-increasing second guard or display latch. |
| September 7 23:59:59 → September 8 00:00:01 with completed day 8 prefetch | Day 8 is adopted through its owner, accepted date/cache identity is day 8, and output is not stale day 7 labeled current. |
| Hold a day 7 request through that forward step | A late response cannot be relabeled day 8. Old completion also cannot release a newer owning request slot. |
| Step backward from day 8 to day 7, then release a pending day 8 response | It can qualify as nextDay when eligible, never as current day 7. Date/Hijri output retains truthful provenance rather than a hidden future hold. |
| Hide, advance fixture wall clock, then show | First resumed callback uses current device time, with one existing eligible acquisition opportunity, not a catch-up storm or second loop. This is simulated visibility evidence, not native sleep. |
| Explicit timeScale=1/60 or frozen simTime, with wall steps | Anchor/rate and existing ADVANCING/forecast/stars/SIM readout behavior remain as declared in the mode table. |

Capture corrected now, current/next labels, selected/loaded dates, cache writes and attempt ownership at each release point, with a crop of actual clock/prayer/date output. Preserve existing valid-scene 325×530 readability, opaque calendar moon, visible live motion, reduced-motion behavior and offscreen pause. No cloud hash may substitute for motion evidence. Native suspend or device-correction claims require actual supported-host observations if later selected; they are not prerequisites to claim only the bounded injected wall-correction pathway with its stated limits.

Mutation controls in an authorized disposable fixture restore the old boot-anchor formula, broaden the default predicate to explicit simTime, and change the loop's `!==` to `>` separately. Default step, explicit frozen, and backward-render cases must respectively fail. Restore the final tree before qualification. A test that mocks nowParts directly cannot qualify whether nowParts consumes the repaired simNow.

## Interfaces, docs, rollback and closure

No new predecessor or graph edge is proposed. Preserve qualification from this owner to [R0007](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/7) and [R0009](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/9), and shared `runtime/clock-mode` / `runtime/render-loop` writes with [R0005](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/5), [R0006](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/6), [R0008](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/8). The request/day fixture consumes existing ownership contracts; it does not transfer their repair scope. One integrator joins overlapping production hunks.

Change only the clock authority predicate/branch, necessary consumer integration, comments and invoked fixtures. Update DESIGN's [one-formula description](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/DESIGN.md#L87-L95) to retain one temporal API with two explicit authorities, and clarify the 1× preview distinction at the existing parameter documentation. No new clock preference, builder field, config/preset migration, installer, dependency, OS setting, active IMPLEMENTAUDIT state or notification feature belongs here.

Rollback the narrow predicate/consumer integration if explicit modes or accepted day behavior regress. Keep the default defect open rather than mask it with a monotonic Hijri clamp. Partial source arithmetic success cannot close #32 while consumer/date/explicit-mode controls fail. Final-tree RED→GREEN/control evidence, independent exact-tree review and browser consumer readback precede an evidence comment and manual closure; use non-closing `Implements #32`. Public repair claims require matching served source/readback. Supplementary historical companion SHA256: `a265910ff3eed52bfb640fabef7ae2c7c35dc24899e364d1349b081c5901c7bf`. No new execution result is asserted by this plan.

Identity provenance: first repository-local allocation batch; existing GitHub object order was used to assign distinct monotonic hex-4 IDs. Closed/held IDs are not reused. Issue number is not implementation priority.

title: R001F: Keep coarse-location deadlines active through response-body parsing
body:
<!-- salah-widget-audit-20260907:SW-031 -->
# R001F: Keep coarse-location deadlines active through response-body parsing

**Repository-local identity:** `R001F` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#31](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/31). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Campaign draft alias: SW-031. Product reliability defect; proposed P2. Scope is coarseDetect's existing two-provider attempt lifetime; this work order grants no implementation or publication authority.

## The timeout ends while the operation is still waiting

The preserved 7 September 2026 source fixture invoked original coarseDetect({timeoutMs:5}) with controlled fetch promises and timers. Both main fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624 and unmerged candidate 9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb produced:

| Step | Preserved result |
|---|---|
| Start GeoJS attempt | One abort timer exists. |
| Resolve HTTP headers with {ok:true,json:()=>pendingBody.promise}; leave body pending; drain microtasks | Abort timers become zero; detection result remains unsettled; fetch count stays one. |
| Release JSON body with latitude "24.47", longitude "39.61", city "Madinah", country_code "SA" | Detection resolves ok:true, provider:"GeoJS", source:"coarse-ip", status:"ok"; cfg has latitude24.47, longitude39.61, method"4", units"c". |

The controlled Intl host supplied America/New_York, which remained cfg.tz in the successful result. This is a timezone-precedence control, not a recommendation about timezone or regional method selection.

The five milliseconds were a configured **virtual timer**, not a measured real-network stall duration. The fixture observed the timer removed before firing; it did not simulate a native browser's abort-aware stream. Releasing only the body recovered the result, isolating the missing deadline to body lifetime. Live outage frequency and actual browser recovery remain unmeasured.

[coarseDetect](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/config.js#L174) starts the timer at line192, then clears it at line194 as soon as fetch resolves headers, before returning r.json(). The outer promise can consequently wait indefinitely with no timer to reach ipinfo. [builder detectArea](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/builder.html#L385) remains at "Detecting your area…"; [widget local boot](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L2190) cannot reach its intended failure/manual-setup branch. These caller consequences follow from the pending promise; the historical fixture did not prove their rendered pixels.

The invariant is: **each provider attempt remains bounded while awaiting headers and body, then either returns its usable result or advances once to the next provider; exhaustion returns explicit failure so the existing manual path can run.** Completion of headers is not completion of detection.

## Re-anchor and preserve the contract

Before authorized implementation, record root, remote, HEAD and dirty state. Expect theislampill/salah_widget; classify relevant drift before editing:

~~~sh
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git remote get-url origin
git rev-parse HEAD
git status --short
git diff fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624 -- config.js builder.html index.html tests/smoke.html
~~~

Stop on incompatible provider, parser or caller changes. The [candidate coarseDetect](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/config.js#L174) has the same historical witness; it is not a prequalified branch to merge.

Write config.js coarseDetect's local next(i) attempt and its narrow regression fixture. Preserve GeoJS→ipinfo order, opts.timeoutMs || 6000, no third attempt, existing fetch options, provider parsing, normalization, source/provider/status fields and timezone precedence. Do not redefine timeoutMs=0, add a new provider or change valid-coordinate/region policy as part of timer repair. Exhaustion must remain {ok:false,source:"coarse-ip",status:"failed"}.

## Minimal staged implementation and observable states

1. Keep the timer alive through fetch→HTTP check→r.json()→provider parsing/normalization. Remove clearTimeout from the headers callback. Successful headers now leave the provider attempt pending with its timer still owned by that attempt.
2. Give timeout a terminal result as well as abort cleanup. Inside next(i), race the full existing local work chain against a local deadline promise. The deadline callback rejects that promise and aborts that attempt's controller. This guarantees logical fallback even if a controlled or noncooperating body promise ignores abort. No global scheduler or reusable transport framework is needed.
3. Clear the attempt's timer only after the race settles. Success returns the existing result; failure clears then invokes next(i+1) once. Never let an old attempt's completion clear the next provider's timer. Keep normalization and result construction local to work; no UI, storage or global config adoption occurs before the winning return.
4. Leave late work attached to handled promises. Its eventual resolution/rejection cannot emit another result, start another fallback or become unhandled. Abort requests transport cleanup; it does not prove a custom transport actually stopped. The attempt can be logically failed while an obsolete noncooperating body remains unresolved.
5. Keep callers' contracts unchanged. Builder can show success/failure using its current intent; widget boot can open manual settings on explicit exhaustion. Any late result arriving after a new form choice must still be rejected by [R000F](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/15). Do not make this timer the form's ownership mechanism.

Design pseudocode for the existing next(i) body, not an executed patch:

~~~js
var ac = new AbortController(), to;
var deadline = new Promise(function (_, reject) {
  to = setTimeout(function () {
    reject(new Error("coarse location timeout"));
    ac.abort();
  }, timeoutMs);
});
var work = Promise.resolve().then(function () {
  return fetch(p.url, {
    signal:ac.signal, mode:"cors",
    referrerPolicy:"no-referrer", cache:"no-store"
  });
}).then(function (r) {
  if (!r.ok) throw new Error("http " + r.status);
  return r.json();
}).then(function (j) {
  // Keep the existing p.parse, coordinate checks, normalize,
  // and success result construction here, unchanged.
  // This chain has no UI/config/storage side effects.
});
return Promise.race([work, deadline]).then(function (result) {
  clearTimeout(to);
  return result;
}, function () {
  clearTimeout(to);
  return next(i + 1);
});
~~~

The final patch must retain the actual parse/return body in the commented position; a missing return is not an implementation. This local race has two real consumers already identified above, so no exported helper or new config field is justified.

Simply moving clearTimeout to final settlement and relying on native fetch abort is a credible smaller alternative **for an abort-aware native Response body**. It must be qualified with the actual stalled-stream browser case. It will not settle the historical abort-ignorant deferred body fixture unless that fixture models abort. The explicit deadline result is chosen here so the promised operation bound remains testable without conflating those two instruments. A fetch-only race repeats the headers/body gap. One global timeout would reduce the fallback provider's existing opportunity; indefinite retry or a new provider expands scope.

Timers cannot preempt synchronous CPU-bound JSON parsing or a blocked event loop. The guarantee is termination of asynchronous waiting once the event loop runs the deadline callback, not a hard wall-clock execution limit through arbitrary synchronous work.

## Public RED/GREEN fixture

Publish the regression source with the later repair. The following proposed fixture invokes actual config.js and supplies the decisive public inputs; it does not require a private audit probe or live provider. Save it as a narrow authorized test and run node tests/coarse-deadline.cjs from the tested checkout:

~~~js
const fs = require("node:fs");
const vm = require("node:vm");
const assert = require("node:assert/strict");
function deferred() {
  let resolve, reject;
  const promise = new Promise((a,b) => { resolve=a; reject=b; });
  return {promise,resolve,reject};
}
const drain = async () => { for (let i=0;i<20;i++) await Promise.resolve(); };
(async () => {
  const timers = new Map(), requests = []; let serial=0;
  const context = {
    URLSearchParams, AbortController, Intl,
    setTimeout(fn,ms) { const id=++serial; timers.set(id,{fn,ms}); return id; },
    clearTimeout(id) { timers.delete(id); },
    fetch(url,opts) {
      const d=deferred(); requests.push({url,opts,...d}); return d.promise;
    }
  };
  context.window=context;
  vm.createContext(context);
  vm.runInContext(fs.readFileSync("config.js","utf8"),context);
  let completions=0;
  const result=context.SalahConfig.coarseDetect({timeoutMs:5})
    .then(value => { completions++; return value; });
  await drain();
  assert.equal(requests.length,1);
  assert.equal(timers.size,1);
  const body=deferred();
  requests[0].resolve({ok:true,json:()=>body.promise});
  await drain();
  // Historical RED: timers.size is 0 here; result is still pending.
  assert.equal(timers.size,1,"deadline must survive headers");
  assert.equal(completions,0);
  const [id,timer]=[...timers.entries()][0];
  assert.equal(timer.ms,5);
  timers.delete(id); timer.fn(); // fire the first provider's virtual deadline
  await drain();
  assert.equal(requests[0].opts.signal.aborted,true);
  assert.equal(requests.length,2,"exactly one fallback");
  requests[1].resolve({ok:true,json:async()=>({
    loc:"51.5,-0.12",city:"London",country:"GB",timezone:"Europe/London"
  })});
  const value=await result;
  assert.equal(value.ok,true); assert.equal(value.provider,"ipinfo");
  assert.equal(value.cfg.lat,51.5); assert.equal(value.cfg.lon,-0.12);
  body.resolve({latitude:"24.47",longitude:"39.61",city:"Madinah",country_code:"SA"});
  await drain();
  assert.equal(completions,1); assert.equal(requests.length,2);
  assert.equal(timers.size,0);
})().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode=1; });
~~~

This is new proposed test text, not a rerun or claimed PASS. It intentionally uses an abort-ignorant body to distinguish timeout-result ownership. Use the exact source's required globals if a later compatible config module needs them; do not replace the production function with test logic. Keep provider fixtures finite/valid, and preserve the historical released-body success as a separate positive control.

| Additional deterministic case | Required final state |
|---|---|
| Healthy GeoJS body before expiry | One request, existing GeoJS success shape, timer removed, no fallback. |
| Headers never resolve | First deadline still advances once to ipinfo. |
| HTTP non-ok, rejected JSON/invalid JSON, or existing parser's unusable-coordinate case | Cleanup then existing fallback; no invented successful location. |
| Both provider attempts reach their virtual deadline | Exactly two requests; result ok:false/source:"coarse-ip"/status:"failed"; no active timers or third request. |
| Body callback settles before deadline; reverse ordering in a separate case | First actual settlement wins. Schedule both explicitly; do not depend on a flaky simultaneous real-time race. |
| Old body rejects after fallback succeeds | No unhandled rejection, duplicate fallback or changed returned result. |
| New form intent during first/fallback attempt | Old result/status cannot alter that form or its saved/exported configuration. |
| Restore clearTimeout at headers in an isolated mutation | The deadline-survives-headers assertion becomes RED again. |
| Remove explicit deadline rejection with abort-ignorant body | Logical-settlement/fallback assertion fails, demonstrating why abort alone is insufficient for this instrument. |

Do not claim the Map timer fixture proves native stream cancellation. The minimum browser bridge serves an isolated local response endpoint that sends successful headers and begins an incomplete JSON body, then withholds the remainder. Redirect the two known provider URLs to local fixture routes before loading config.js, while retaining native fetch/AbortController/Response body behavior. First route stalls; second returns the healthy ipinfo body above. Observe first-request abort, one fallback, result and cleanup. Add a finite streamed GeoJS control. Close only fixture-owned requests/server resources afterward; never induce a real provider outage.

Finally invoke actual builder detectArea and a fresh disposable widget #local=1 boot. Two provider failures must produce the builder's manual/precise recovery guidance and the widget's manual settings/render-loop path. Capture the relevant UI crop; a helper's return value alone cannot prove usable manual recovery. No host storage or geolocation prompt is needed. Native browser/event-loop version and fixture identity belong in the evidence; a Node result cannot certify a specific embedding host.

## Integration, compatibility, rollback and closure

The sole repair domain remains config/coarse-detection. Its existing qualification edge from [R000F](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/15) is unchanged. [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3) owns remote request/config adoption, [R0006](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/6) prayer liveness, [R000D](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/13) weather/radar transport and [R0011](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/17) settings reset feedback. Similar timeout needs do not justify merging these owners or adding a global transport abstraction. No relationship delta is proposed.

Builder/index are consumer tests; edit them only for a demonstrated necessary caller-contract adjustment. Preserve successful source/provider/accuracy/area fields, timezone and country mapping, local/hash/saved priority, v1 saved configuration, cache compatibility and all installer/preset payloads. Keep 325×530 layout, header/footer readability and ordinary visual behavior. README recovery wording changes only if the actual repaired behavior requires clarification; no "bounded operation" or public recovery claim before its readback.

Rollback timer/race/fallback edits as one coherent unit if healthy detection regresses. Do not retain only a header-time cleanup while declaring the deadline fixed. Stop on incompatible caller/provider drift or an unapproved broader transport design. Source-only or virtual-only evidence remains partial where native/browser recovery is claimed.

DONE requires final integrated-tree RED→GREEN, positive/boundary/mutation controls, the native streamed-body and actual-caller checks, and independent exact-tree review of cleanup and one-fallback ownership. Add an evidence comment binding tree, fixture, schedules, outcomes and limits. Public claims additionally require matching served config.js/callers and the recovery readback. Use non-closing Implements #31 PR wording and manual closure after evidence. This work order asserts no executed product or independent PASS.

Identity provenance: first repository-local allocation batch; existing GitHub object order was used to assign distinct monotonic hex-4 IDs. Closed/held IDs are not reused. Issue number is not implementation priority.

title: R001E: Allow valid equator and prime-meridian coordinates to reach weather and radar acquisition
body:
<!-- salah-widget-audit-20260907:SW-030 -->
# R001E — Preserve valid zero-axis coordinates at weather/radar dispatch

**Repository-local identity:** `R001E` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#30](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/30). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Campaign draft alias: SW-030. Existing tracker: https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/30. Priority P2; corrective input-domain repair. This work order changes two acquisition guards, not prayer-provider policy, location selection or weather calibration. It does not authorize implementation, commit or deployment by itself.

## Re-anchor the actual target

The observed main baseline is `fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624`; audit branch `9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb` has the same relevant guards and is evidence, not a merge instruction. Main `index.html` SHA256 is `446453b522f56f5f1bc0afd1a3abd09b73756754fa58a6b3b0ff09ce953a2eec`; audit SHA256 is `464f8eef80a67f337cb0e323b8b79a90b7c445ff57a9c38cb3497eec729f4ef2`.

Before an authorized repair, run `git remote -v`, `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, and `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all`. Confirm this is `theislampill/salah_widget`, preserve unrelated work and compare the current `index.html`, `config.js` and `tests/smoke.html` against the pinned main. Re-anchor the functions below by name if lines moved. Stop for reconciliation if another owner has already changed coordinate capture, admission or dispatch; do not blindly apply the old hunk.

Public source owners:

- [`fetchWeather`, including its guard and query construction](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L771-L779).
- [`fetchRadar`, manifest dispatch and tile construction](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L816-L840).
- [`SalahConfig.normalize` and `validate`](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/config.js#L69-L100), which already admit numeric zero.
- [`tests/smoke.html`](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/tests/smoke.html), the integration-test owner; changes must retain required-test accounting and storage isolation.

## Incident and evidence limits

A controlled-source audit executed the actual bounded `fetchWeather` and `fetchRadar` functions from both pinned trees, with recorded fetch/Image/canvas/storage stand-ins and a fixed clock. It also ran the real configuration normalization/validation. The decisive results were:

| Runtime latitude, longitude | Configuration valid | Combined weather + radar-manifest dispatches |
|---|---:|---:|
|0,30|yes|0|
|30,0|yes|0|
|0,0|yes|0|
|0.000001,30|yes|2|

The nonzero control distinguishes coordinate truthiness from a general network, busy-state or fixture failure. Both axes are independently causal. This is exact-source dispatch evidence; the original zero fixture's fetch stand-in returned an empty object, so it does not prove weather payload admission, successful radar image loading, live coverage or correct rendered conditions.

The causal chain is short but consequential: valid numeric zero enters runtime state → `!lat || !lon` treats zero as absent → acquisition returns before building/issuing either request → no provider has an opportunity to answer. Changing only the configuration validator cannot repair this because validation already succeeded. The defect can affect a valid equator or prime-meridian location independently of its climate or selected calculation method.

A separate dated Aladhan observation must not be conflated with this local gate. On2026-09-07, the timings endpoint for07-09-2026, method2/school0 returned HTTP400 for `(0,0)`, `(0,-78.4678)` and `(51.4769,0)`;0.01-degree neighbours returned HTTP200 in the recorded follow-up, while reported0.000001-degree neighbours did not. Those are historical prayer-provider snapshots, not a current or permanent service guarantee. This issue neither fixes that provider nor authorizes moving the user's coordinates. A successful weather repair must not be advertised as complete zero-axis prayer support.

## Intended invariant and smallest repair

For already normalized runtime coordinates, an eligible acquisition accepts finite numeric latitude in[-90,90] and longitude in[-180,180], including positive and negative zero. It rejects absent, nonnumeric, nonfinite and out-of-domain direct runtime values. Coordinate validity remains separate from busy, simulation and retry/throttle eligibility; those clauses keep their existing behavior.

Replace only the two truthiness predicates with the existing usable-coordinate contract if one is actually shared at the repair head, otherwise a small local predicate equivalent to:

```js
const usableCoordinates = (la, lo) =>
  typeof la === 'number' && Number.isFinite(la) && la >= -90 && la <= 90 &&
  typeof lo === 'number' && Number.isFinite(lo) && lo >= -180 && lo <= 180;
```

This is proposed design, not a shipped helper. Both real acquisition call paths must consume it; merely exporting or unit-testing an unused helper does not repair dispatch. If [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3) has established immutable request context, validate and construct the request from that same captured coordinate pair. Do not validate one global pair then issue with a later different pair.

Keep existing query serialization, units/timezone parameters, manifest address and tile geometry. Do not replace coordinates with epsilon, convert valid zero to a fallback place, broaden network retry, add a provider, alter calculation methods or change the persisted configuration schema.

An important compatibility boundary: the current `normalize` intentionally clamps some raw out-of-range values. The preserved normalizer controls include100/200→90/180 and Infinity/-Infinity→90/-180. Therefore direct-runtime negative guard cases below do **not** assert that all raw form/hash inputs must now be rejected. The normal configuration path retains its established coercion/clamping behavior. A raw hash string`"0"` may normalize to numeric0; the runtime predicate does not need to accept arbitrary unnormalized strings. Changing that normalization policy is a different owner decision.

## Construct a deterministic RED without private files or live services

Use an isolated test harness, never the owner's stored settings or public origin. Execute the actual functions from the checked-out source with controlled dependencies; copied guard logic alone is not the RED. A VM/fixture harness may expose these two functions and the runtime variables without executing boot or real network calls. Keep that fixture's extraction/entry boundary explicit and fail if either real function is missing.

Set `Date.now()` to `Date.parse('2026-09-07T21:00:00Z')`, `SIM.wx=null`, `ADVANCING=false`, units`c`, timezone`UTC`, weather/track/radar state empty, busy flags false and last-attempt/success clocks0. Recreate all state for every coordinate pair. Replace fetch with a recorder that appends the actual URL and returns a resolved fake response; provide inert Image/canvas/storage dependencies. Await weather and radar invocation settlement rather than assuming one microtask is enough.

Invoke `fetchWeather()` and `fetchRadar()` once for each table row. Baseline expected RED: the three zero-axis pairs dispatch nothing; the tiny nonzero control dispatches two requests. Record the actual function/source identity and observed calls. If the nonzero control fails, repair the harness or classify environmental/ownership drift before claiming the product defect reproduced.

For the corrected guard discriminator, assert actual weather query values, not a URL reconstructed from input after the fact:

```js
const u = new URL(recordedWeatherRequest);
assert.equal(u.origin + u.pathname, 'https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast');
assert.equal(u.searchParams.get('latitude'), String(expectedLatitude));
assert.equal(u.searchParams.get('longitude'), String(expectedLongitude));
assert.equal(u.searchParams.get('wind_speed_unit'), 'ms');
```

Zero must serialize as`"0"`; no epsilon is permitted. Temperature-unit/timezone assertions must reflect the actual captured config and any accepted sibling change. The first radar request is exactly`https://api.rainviewer.com/public/weather-maps.json`; it has no coordinate query parameters. Coordinate preservation for radar is proved at its subsequent tile request.

Extend that same harness with a healthy status200 radar manifest:

```js
const nowSec = Date.parse('2026-09-07T21:00:00Z') / 1000;
const manifest = {
  generated: nowSec,
  host: 'https://tilecache.rainviewer.com',
  radar: { past: [{ time: nowSec, path: '/v2/radar/' + nowSec }] }
};
```

Have the fake Image capture its assigned `src` and settle predictably with an inert canvas. The current tile path is`host + path + '/256/6/' + xt + '/' + yt + '/2/1_1.png'`. Independently compute integer Web-Mercator indices at zoom6; proposed expected controls are `(0,30)→(37,32)`, `(30,0)→(32,26)` and `(0,0)→(32,32)`. Verify those expectations when constructing the fixture; no saved audit execution of these full tile controls is claimed. Do not assert that a fake image proves real precipitation, calibration or tile coverage.

## Ordered implementation and integration

1. Re-anchor source and retain the three REDs plus their nonzero control. Record normalization separately from acquisition.
2. Replace both local guard predicates, preserving every other eligibility clause. If sharing a tiny predicate, prove both functions reach it and it consumes the same request context as URL/tile construction.
3. Run actual dispatch/query and healthy-manifest tile controls, then direct-invalid/busy/SIM/throttle controls. A state where weather accepts zero but radar still returns early is partial, not done.
4. Join the shared weather/radar hunks through one source integrator with [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3), [R000B](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/11), [R000C](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/12), [R000D](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/13) and [R000E](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/14). This is a shared-write constraint, not a whole-issue blocking predecessor. Data admission, source age, bounded attempt cleanup and radar authority retain their existing owners.
5. Run one disposable-origin browser acquisition/consumer fixture using a healthy response conforming to the actual weather admission contract at that combined head. Check the consumed header condition and `.c.dataset.fx` at a zero-axis location. No live provider is needed to qualify local dispatch. Keep unavailable prayer data explicitly unavailable if the independent prayer path rejects the location.
6. Re-run existing relevant smoke controls and retain source/response/URL/image/consumer receipts. Preserve fixed325×530 composition, header/footer visibility and existing moon/motion behavior; this predicate repair provides no new renderer-art PASS.

## Acceptance matrix and false-green controls

| Case | Required final evidence | False green rejected |
|---|---|---|
|Each of the three zero-axis pairs|One weather and one manifest request per independent eligible fixture; exact coordinate strings|Configuration validation alone, or testing only one axis|
|Ordinary and tiny nonzero controls|Existing dispatch remains eligible|A harness that suppressed all requests|
|Direct null/undefined/NaN/±Infinity or range violation|No dispatch from invalid runtime state|Truthiness replacement that admits every nonzero value|
|String`"0"` through real config normalization|Numeric0 reaches acquisition|Accidentally redefining accepted hash input as invalid|
|Busy, explicit simulated weather, existing cooldown|Existing duplicate/forbidden request suppression remains|Bypassing the rest of either guard to obtain a green zero test|
|Captured context changes mid-request|URL and later radar tile use the dispatched coordinate pair|Guard checks old pair but tile reads new globals|
|Healthy manifest|Actual assigned tile URL has the correct zoom6 indices and unchanged zero coordinate geometry|Asserting a separately constructed expected URL without observing Image.src|
|One zero-axis healthy weather response|Real browser consumer sees admitted current fixture data|Network recorder count reported as successful rendering|
|Independent mutants|Restoring old truthiness in weather alone fails weather zero controls; restoring it in radar alone fails radar controls|A combined assertion that never reaches one function|
|Prayer-provider failure|Weather dispatch can pass while prayer support remains explicitly unproved/unavailable|Epsilon location changes or blanket support claims|

Run negative/mutation controls in an isolated authorized fixture or review worktree. The owner's application checkout and browser settings must not become a test scratchpad. Historical RED evidence is already available, but all proposed corrected and mutation outcomes require actual future execution before implementation closure.

## Alternatives, public effects, rollback and closure

Input truthiness is the wrong abstraction for geographical coordinates. Epsilon substitution changes the requested place and still lacks a reliable provider guarantee. A configuration-only “allow zero” patch misses both real early returns. Removing the entire guard risks overlap with busy/throttle/simulation and request-ownership protections. A broad acquisition refactor or new validation library has substantially more regression surface than these two predicates.

IMPLEMENTAUDIT R001D: the affected shipped source is`index.html`; integration tests own actual dispatch/consumer evidence. `config.js` is a compatibility control unless the current-head contract requires a narrowly reconciled caller change. No builder format, preset, installer, dependency or generated artifact changes are expected. Update README/help only if an existing support claim would otherwise overstate prayer-provider behavior; the documentation integrator owns shared prose. Public/Pages source readback is required only when a later authorized deployment is claimed, not as evidence that this work order was filed.

Stop on conflicting request-context changes, failed nonzero controls, invalid-coordinate requests, altered normalized coordinates or a broader provider-policy requirement. If the narrow guard change causes a regression, revert only that change in the authorized implementation workspace and retain the failing control; do not “recover” by silently moving the location. A rollback may reinstate the known zero-dispatch defect and must be reported as such, not as successful functional repair.

Done requires both acquisition owners repaired, final-tree RED→GREEN plus controls/mutants recorded, shared-hunk integration reviewed, and actual bounded browser consumer evidence separated from live service limitations. Missing radar or invalid-input coverage is partial completion. Use a non-closing `Implements #30` link for a future authorized PR; publish an evidence comment before manual issue closure. No implementation, PR, deployment or closure is performed by this publication campaign.

The invariant is distinct from weather response validity, liveness, age and calibration: valid location0must reach eligible dispatch. Preserved weather W001 and the dated provider zero-axis observations supply provenance; their decision-relevant inputs and limits are included above so a cold executor does not need the private campaign archive.

Methodology references (separate repository, not Salah work owners): [R001D in IMPLEMENTAUDIT](https://github.com/theislampill/IMPLEMENTAUDIT.md/issues/155).

Identity provenance: first repository-local allocation batch; existing GitHub object order was used to assign distinct monotonic hex-4 IDs. Closed/held IDs are not reused. Issue number is not implementation priority.

title: R001D: Bind lunar diagnostics to consumed state and current canvas geometry
body:
<!-- salah-widget-audit-20260907:SW-029 -->
# R001D: Bind lunar diagnostics to consumed state and current canvas geometry

**Repository-local identity:** `R001D` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#29](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/29). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Two existing moon instruments can give a false result: freshness is recomputed after consumption and treats missing observation as fresh; the pixel overlay samples an obsolete radius and mislabels interior pixels as limb/exterior. Repair those instruments and their negative controls while preserving the moon's default appearance and update cadence. This issue does not assert that shipped moon pixels are stale or visually wrong.

Campaign draft alias: SW-029. Existing GitHub owner: #29. P2, instrument/acceptance defect with two already accepted subcases. No shader redesign, lunar orientation feature, optical-physics claim or new visual objective is included. Publication of this work order is not execution authority.

## Bound owners and preservation checks

Historical main: `fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624`; candidate: `9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb`. Before an authorized implementation record `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `git remote get-url origin`, `git status --short`, `git rev-parse HEAD`, then inspect `git diff fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624 -- index.html tests/smoke.html AGENTS.md DESIGN.md`. Confirm `theislampill/salah_widget`, preserve unrelated work and stop on incompatible moon-state/caller drift. Never dump or replace the embedded bitmap while inspecting these owners.

Exact source owners: [main backing dimensions `_MN/_MR`](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L953), [`renderMoon()` state replacement and DEBUGMOON sampler](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L1024), [minute update and `applyTheme()` call](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L1982), [pure atmosphere freshness field](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L1759), [QA projection](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L2040), and [existing smoke assertion](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/tests/smoke.html#L151). Candidate equivalents include [state/update](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/index.html#L2009) and [QA projection](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/index.html#L2165).

## A: Freshness can describe a later update instead of the frame

The original production order updates moon geometry before `applyTheme(M)` and passed the retained positive control. The counterexample deliberately reordered a consumer in an exact-source fixture; it is not evidence that production already consumes stale pixels.

The saved source-slice fixture began with `M.nowMin=60`, `lastMoonMin=59`, `moonSky={alt:4,frac:0.5,up:1,_min:59}`. A controlled `renderMoon()` replaced geometry with altitude 5 and the caller then wrote `_min=60`. Actual results were identical on both bound trees:

| Source-slice sequence | State actually consumed | Later QA / warnings |
|---|---|---|
| Update+stamp, then consume | altitude 5, fresh=true | 0 warnings; positive control |
| Consume, then update+stamp | altitude 4, fresh=false | `qaAfterReorder=true`, 0 warnings — false GREEN |
| Omit update+stamp | altitude 4, fresh=false | 1 warning — narrower negative does discriminate |
| Update, then direct `renderMoon()` replacement outside render | altitude 5, `_min` absent | 1 warning despite freshly replaced geometry |
| QA projection with `A={}` | No observation | `moonSkyFresh=true`; explicit `{moonSkyFresh:false}` returns false |

Mechanism: `atmosphere(M)` compares the live `moonSky._min` with the current minute. `qaState()` recomputes atmosphere later, then projects `(A.moonSkyFresh!==false)`. A post-consumption update erases evidence of what the frame used, and an empty object passes the not-false expression. Meanwhile `renderMoon()` replaces the object without a stamp; only one caller stamps it. Boot/config/day-adoption callers can replace the object without coherent metadata.

The repair must bind three distinct facts: geometry produced for a given time/context, the state consumed by `paint`, and whether that observation completed. Proposed implementation:

1. Make stamp ownership part of producing `moonSky` inside `renderMoon()`, using the same captured `date=simDate()` and location context that produced geometry. Keep its existing no-argument callers valid. Preserve the existing minute field where consumed, but include enough time identity to distinguish the same minute-of-day on different dates; derive the absolute minute from the captured date rather than inventing elapsed time from render count. Invalidate appropriately on location changes, and do not claim fresh solely because a minute number happens to match after an unqualified state replacement.
2. Retain minute cadence and the PBR phase/raster cache. A fresh geometry computation does not require a new raster if its phase remains within the existing cache threshold. Stamp only after successful geometry production; a failed update must not advance `lastMoonMin` into a false-success state. Keep errors nonthrowing at the public diagnostic boundary and preserve existing render behavior.
3. At `applyTheme(M)`'s actual `atmosphere(M) → paint(A)` boundary, capture a small immutable value snapshot of the freshness result and the produced/expected time/context actually being consumed. Commit the last-consumed diagnostic only for the corresponding paint attempt; distinguish failure/unavailable from a completed paint. Reuse the existing last-render-summary idiom, not a global event log. An update later in the tick cannot rewrite this snapshot.
4. Have the freshness member exposed by `qaState().moonTruth` read that last consumed snapshot. Other existing QA fields may retain their present computations, but clearly separate “current recomputed state” from “last consumed frame” if both are shown. Before the first successful observation, or after a failed observation for the latest attempt, freshness is unavailable—not true. Preserve a strict `===true` success assertion; explicit false/stale and null/unavailable must both fail an attempted-fresh acceptance test. Do not make a missing diagnostic pass merely to avoid smoke noise.
5. Keep `atmosphere()` pure. Move any bounded warning to the captured consumption result rather than checking only after a possibly reordered update. Preserve direct QA calls and opt-in diagnostics; do not add per-frame hard exceptions, a new scheduler, or a persisted diagnostic schema.

These are proposed internal metadata choices, not claims that new fields already exist. Record exact production/consumption identity in test results so a cold reviewer can distinguish a stale frame from a newly produced but not yet consumed state.

## B: Pixel labels refer to the old moon radius

The backing canvas is `_MN=300`, `_MR=144`; the DEBUGMOON try-body uses `N=_moonCv.width,R=58,cx=N/2,cy=N/2`. Its sampler calculates `x=round(cx+f*R)` and flattens `(y*N+x)*4` without checking x/y. The five labels use factors 0.5, 0.99, 1.0, 1.04 and 1.25. With R=58, all are in the current disc's interior.

The preserved deterministic image definition is public and requires no private texture:

```javascript
const width = 300, height = 300, radius = 144;
const data = new Uint8ClampedArray(width * height * 4);
for (let y = 0; y < height; y++) {
  for (let x = 0; x < width; x++) {
    const r = Math.hypot(x - width / 2, y - height / 2);
    const i = (y * width + x) * 4;
    if (r <= radius) {
      data[i] = data[i + 1] = data[i + 2] = r < 100 ? 255 : 0;
      data[i + 3] = 255;
    }
  }
}
```

The exact source sampler, supplied this synthetic `getImageData().data`, reported `inner 255/255  limb 255/255  edge 255/255  out 255/255  sky 255/255` on both trees. Radius-144 plus bounds-check control reported inner 255/255, limb/edge 0/255, out/sky out-of-bounds. Independently `(x=299,y=150)` had alpha 0. This source/VM evidence does not test the real texture, DOM or compositor and makes no claim that the rendered Moon is transparent or black.

Simply replacing 58 with 144 is incomplete: `round(150+1.04*144)=300`, outside a 300-pixel row. A flat array access can then read a different row while remaining inside the buffer. Required sampler repair:

1. Read width and height from the actual canvas; use the shared renderer radius `_MR` and matching center. Keep the backing raster, texture and CSS moon size unchanged.
2. Check integer x/y against width/height **before** calculating the flattened index. Out-of-bounds returns explicit unavailable/OOB, not a clamp presented as the originally named point. Handle absent canvas/context/image data without throwing or reporting a good sample.
3. Retain meaningful inner/limb/edge positions with their coordinates. For an actual just-outside-disc sample, choose a valid pixel beyond the shared radius, e.g. `(ceil(cx+R)+1,cy)=(295,150)` for this geometry, only if in bounds. A valid farther canvas-exterior control is `(299,150)`. If no such pixel exists, say unavailable. The raw transparent canvas is not the composited sky: name that measurement “canvas exterior” or explicitly qualify the old sky label.
4. Expose coordinates/radius/dimensions with the opt-in readout so its labels are auditable. Do not introduce extra default-frame `getImageData()` work or use diagnostic numbers to replace required composited moon crops.

## Final-tree controls that must distinguish the defects

| Subcase/control | Required result |
|---|---|
| Normal actual render update-before-consume | Completed consumed snapshot is fresh; no false warning. Test real `applyTheme/paint` reachability in an isolated full-render harness. |
| Consumer-before-update mutant | Captured consumed snapshot remains stale after the later update; current-state QA must not turn it into fresh. This must fail the actual freshness smoke. |
| Omitted update; empty/throwing atmosphere; failed paint; pre-first-render query | Explicit stale or unavailable as applicable, never PASS. Assert which stage ran rather than accepting an empty projection. |
| Same-minute reuse and direct `renderMoon()` callers | Reuse remains fresh when time/context matches; boot, cache/network day adoption and location application preserve stamp ownership after object replacement. Exercise same minute-of-day on a different date and a location change so equal minute numbers cannot mask context drift. |
| Synthetic image above | Inner bright/opaque, limb and edge dark/opaque, valid exterior alpha 0, with correct coordinates. |
| Bright-disc positive image | Actual sampled in-disc regions report their bright values; no hardcoded “dark limb” result. |
| Bounds `(300,150)`, negative x/y and `y=height` | Explicit OOB/unavailable; no row wrapping or adjacent-buffer interpretation. Empty/error image read is unavailable. |
| Mutations | Restore `R=58`: dark-limb/exterior fixture fails. Remove coordinate bounds: OOB case fails. Restore `!==false` or recompute after consumption: freshness negatives fail. |

The source-slice results above are historical. Proposed whole-render, error, context and final-browser controls are not executed PASS. Keep the retained source-slice negative as a fast discriminator, but do not substitute it for actual consumer integration. Preserve tested PBR cache behavior: 0.001 phase change reused its raster/buffer in the historical control, whereas 0.006 repainted with reused storage. Those controls do not measure real GPU cost or prove visual beauty.

Inspect representative final composited moon crops and debug labels to ensure the diagnostic-only repair changes no appearance: opaque disc through crescent/half/gibbous/full, faint opaque new/below-horizon calendar disc with no invented moonlight, existing Earthshine and normal frame placement. Do not claim a visual improvement from corrected instrumentation. If rendering changes or a visual regression appears, stop this diagnostic closure and qualify that exact effect separately. Live motion remains a real-time crop/delta gate; cloud hashes are not motion evidence.

## Integration, public effects and rollback

`HE-R1-06-F1` owns consumed-freshness fidelity; `HXP-F001` owns sampler geometry. They remain two subcases under this one already accepted instrument owner, not new issues. Domains are `runtime/moon-diagnostics` and `test/moon-instruments`. There is no new declared predecessor or relationship delta. Coordinate exact `renderMoon`/`applyTheme` and smoke hunks through the shared writer; nearby date/clock work does not grant authority to rewrite those systems.

title: R001C: Make optical and motion diagnostic recipes match the actual hash parser and force options
body:
<!-- salah-widget-audit-20260907:SW-028 -->
# R001C: Make optical and motion diagnostic recipes match the actual hash parser and force options

**Repository-local identity:** `R001C` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#28](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/28). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Campaign draft alias: SW-028. Diagnostic-documentation defect; proposed P2. This work order repairs existing recipes, including AGENTS.md; it grants no implementation or publication authority.

## The literal recipes fail their stated purpose

The preserved 7 September 2026 controlled-source check recorded the same result on main fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624 and unmerged candidate 9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb:

| Exact public fixture URL | Parsed debugMotion |
|---|---|
| https://example.invalid/?debugMotion=1#lat=24.4672&lon=39.6142 | null |
| https://example.invalid/#lat=24.4672&lon=39.6142&debugMotion=1 | "1" |

This was original-source hash parsing in a controlled Node VM, not browser motion or optical-pixel evidence. [index.html:593](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L593) constructs q from location.hash.slice(1); it never reads the query for these options. A contributor can therefore follow a literal ?debugMotion or ?motion recipe while the claimed override remains inactive.

The [optical switch](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L1718) accepts exactly **halo, sundogs, pillar, anticrep, paraselene, lunarhalo**. It does not individually force corona, earthshine, refraction or the crepuscular ray. A parsed unsupported string is not an implemented force branch.

DESIGN already says configuration is hash-based; that is a real contrary control and limits severity. It does not repair its copyable query-style examples or "Each can be forced" statement. The same faulty syntax occurs in AGENTS's motion-auditor/M0/forbidden-regression instructions. Correcting only DESIGN and OPTICS would leave the failure in contributor guidance.

## Re-anchor and make the exact small documentation edit

Before authorized editing, record repository root, remote, HEAD and dirty paths. Expect theislampill/salah_widget; do not infer the defect persists on arbitrary future HEAD.

~~~sh
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git remote get-url origin
git rev-parse HEAD
git status --short
git diff fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624 -- AGENTS.md DESIGN.md OPTICS.md index.html
~~~

Stop on incompatible parser/enum changes and revise the affected recipe from that evidence. The candidate is comparison evidence, not an adoption instruction: [candidate parser](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/index.html#L593).

One documentation integrator owns these edits:

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/AGENTS.md): replace affected ?debugMotion/?motion examples in the auditor, M0 and forbidden-regression prose. Keep the existing base-hash-plus-& convention in Running/debugging and all screenshot/no-cloud-hash gates.
- [DESIGN.md motion/debug section](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/DESIGN.md#L223): repair query-style examples; include lunarhalo in the enum near line258. Replace the all-effects force claim in [the approximations section](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/DESIGN.md#L318).
- [OPTICS.md](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/OPTICS.md#L99): correct query-style headings and the validation-matrix recipe. index.html remains a verification owner only.

Use this exact explanatory text with the runnable examples below:

> Configuration and diagnostics are read from the fragment after #. Append &debugMotion=1 or &motion=full to that same fragment. A query-only ?debugMotion=1 is not read. The six debugOptic force names are halo, sundogs, pillar, anticrep, paraselene and lunarhalo. Corona, earthshine, refraction and the crepuscular ray require controlled physical scene inputs; no dedicated debugOptic switch forces them.

Replace "Each can be forced via ?debugOptic=" with the six-name statement. Do not globally rewrite question marks: builder's cache-busting query is intentional, and negative examples must stay visibly labeled negative.

Use these complete motion recipes, relative to the served folder:

~~~text
index.html#lat=24.47&lon=39.61&label=Madinah&method=4&debugMotion=1
index.html#lat=24.47&lon=39.61&label=Madinah&method=4&debugMotion=1&motion=full
~~~

For a copyable force-activation example use:

~~~text
index.html#lat=24.47&lon=39.61&label=Madinah&method=4&simTime=12:30&debugOptic=halo
~~~

For other switch branches, replace only halo with a supported name and select a recorded solar/lunar scene appropriate to its pixel check. The noon example proves neither lunar visibility nor every effect's appearance. State: **"simTime without timeScale freezes the clock-driven scene. Use the real-time recipe above for a 15–60 second motion check. Flag activation alone does not prove visible motion or correct optical pixels."**

A vague hash reminder without fixing literal URLs is insufficient. Adding query parsing or force-everything branches changes runtime behavior to vindicate old prose. A renderer overhaul or new diagnostic framework is unnecessary for this exact documentation failure.

## Public discriminator and validation

For each changed literal URL, use this small proposed fixture and compare it with the actual source q expression at the bound tree:

~~~js
function parsed(recipe) {
  const u = new URL(recipe, "https://example.invalid/");
  return new URLSearchParams(u.hash.slice(1));
}
const bad = "index.html?debugMotion=1#lat=24.4672&lon=39.6142";
const good = "index.html#lat=24.4672&lon=39.6142&debugMotion=1";
if (parsed(bad).get("debugMotion") !== null) throw Error("negative control");
if (parsed(good).get("debugMotion") !== "1") throw Error("fragment recipe");
~~~

This is proposed recipe validation, not an executed test result. Include every changed AGENTS/DESIGN/OPTICS occurrence in the readback. For motion=full examples assert the parsed value is "full"; compare all six claimed force names against the real DEBUGOPTIC branches. Negative controls: move the positive flag before # and the positive assertion must fail; propose corona as an implemented branch and the enum comparison must fail even though q can contain the string "corona". Do not test only a manually corrected URL while leaving a broken published example unexamined.

Then open the actual complete real-time recipe on a disposable local browser origin and confirm the production q value and debugMotion readout are active. A visual claim additionally needs an actual 15–60 second watch/clip or diagnostic delta and the relevant crop, performed by one browser owner. **Never use qaState().clouds.hash as motion proof.** Full motion under OS reduced-motion requires the explicit motion=full case and its readback; normal mode retains accessibility reduction.

This issue qualifies syntax and advertised forceability. For physically driven effects without dedicated switches, retain the existing physical-scene requirements and identify their fixture inputs when claiming pixels; do not invent a passing fixture here. Keep visible-corner-sun registration, opaque calendar moon, fixed325×530/readability and fail-closed painted dawn unchanged.

## Boundaries, rollback and closure

The accepted AGENTS-owner correction remains included. No typed-edge or write-domain delta is proposed; shared guidance changes stay with the documentation integrator. No index/builder/config behavior, installer, preset, permission or regional-policy change is required. README changes only if an affected link needs correction.

Revert inaccurate recipe text if validation fails while retaining correct hash/enum statements. Stop if current source exposes different options or the required browser readback is unavailable; parser-only evidence remains parser-only. DONE requires exact final text, literal-recipe/enum controls and an evidence comment; published-document claims also require rendered public readback. Use non-closing Implements #28 PR wording and manual closure after evidence. This work order is not an independent PASS or a runtime repair.
