Final whole-file parsing is separately required by [R0014](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/20).

## Repair order and preview data flow

**1. Fix the entry boundary first.** Parse/validate options and platform before creating any directory. For preview, perform read-only local target discovery, mark legacy profiles as refused, print intended per-target actions and terminate without entering the installation loop. Do not require a person to pretend they installed an extension by pressing Enter. A no-terminal preview can enumerate all detected eligible targets; an `ask` source prints both available routes as unresolved alternatives. No target/no eligible target remains an explicit non-success planning result. Keep this branch small and local to each existing main entry point; it is not a generic plan/execution engine.

Choose offline behavior for the existing switch: no metadata requests, no provider requests, no download and no implicit DNS/network availability test. If the owner later wants an online read-only preview, that requires a separately explicit product option and contract; do not silently allow it here. Say “release/version/path unresolved until execution” rather than fabricate a current tag, a cache hit or a completed download. The preview can show a proposed directory template but may not create one to learn its random suffix.

**2. Guard each effect site as defense against alternate callers.** The early branch is the main consumer boundary; helpers remain independently guarded so cached/fallback paths or a future caller cannot bypass it. Check DryRun before mkdir, copy, remove, unzip/Expand-Archive, permission changes, file writes, clipboard, open/process launch and cleanup. `copy_text`/`Copy-Text` must return a result that does not trigger “Copied” output when suppressed. Choose false/no-copy with a preview diagnostic; a dry-run success boolean would lie to existing callers. Guard `select_asset`/`Get-LatestRelease` before even an existing metadata cache is interpreted as authority for effects.

**3. Stop passing imagined artifacts down real paths.** `download_tablissng_asset`, `Download-Asset` and preset helpers must not return a pretend success path under preview. The entry preview prints the plan itself, bypassing actual artifact-returning helpers. If a guarded helper is invoked during dry-run, return no usable path and a documented suppressed result/diagnostic; callers must stop that operation rather than expand, copy or fall back to opening a store. Normal helper success retains the existing path contract. This avoids introducing a new persisted result schema solely for dry-run.

**4. Join private staging before the final gate.** [R0015](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/21) creates separate scratch and retained roots. Dry-run must not call its initializer, create a retained bundle, chmod a parent, adopt an old cache, or run cleanup. Cleanup is an effect too; a guard that stops writes but runs a trap deleting cached/manual assets is a failure. Integrate shared `bash/staging`, `bash/preset-write`, `bash/unpacked-lifetime` and `bash/download-return` hunks serially with the installer owner. [R0013](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/19)’s actual-input repair applies to normal installation; agree explicitly that preview does not wait for terminal confirmations.

**5. Make completion wording reflect the mode.** End preview with “Preview only; no changes made” only after the no-effect controls pass. List planned opens/copies/imports with “would”, retain the legacy-profile refusal and dashboard replacement warning, and state which remote facts remain unresolved. Normal execution still distinguishes staged files from manual browser installation/import. A swallowed selector failure or an empty selected set cannot become successful install text.

## Whole-entry acceptance: branch and effect matrix

Build isolated fixtures with actual source entry points, fake profile discovery and effect spies. Snapshot the fixture filesystem before/after, including preexisting cached ZIP/XPI, unpacked marker and preset sentinels; hash contents and record names/modes. Place spy logs outside the snapshot target and distinguish harness-created fixture files from installer effects. Deny network at the test transport boundary. Avoid the owner’s browser storage/profiles and real clipboard. A missing spy hit alone is insufficient if a direct .NET write escaped interception; the snapshot and network denial are the independent post-state controls.

| Branch/control | Required observation under dry-run |
|---|---|
| Fresh GitHub Chromium/Firefox | No metadata/download/extraction/clipboard/open; unresolved tag explicitly shown. |
| Cached asset + cached metadata; preexisting unpacked directory | Same zero effects; cached files and directory sentinels byte-identical; no cached shortcut to expansion. |
| Store route; source `ask`; GitHub metadata error/fallback | Plan only, no browser process, no “after installed” confirmation, no network; unresolved choice stays unresolved. |
| Already-installed TablissNG; missing preset URL; existing configured preset | No preset download/rewrite/copy; manual import/replacement warning remains understandable. |
| Legacy-only, mixed eligible/legacy, zero profiles, malformed options | Refusal/error is explicit and no-effect; eligible plans exclude legacy; no staged-completion claim. |
| NO_OPEN/NoOpen alone, dry-run off | Only opening is suppressed. The fixture still logs expected download/staging/copy, proving the tests distinguish switches. |
| Non-dry positive, effects stubbed | Expected normal branches reach the spies with exact arguments and configuration; the repair has not disabled installation globally. |
| Mutants: remove eager-init guard, return cached path early, copy during preview, cleanup on EXIT | Each targeted case detects a specific call or changed sentinel; a fresh-only fixture cannot pass the cache mutant. |

Run Bash on the claimed Apple Bash 3.2 and modern Linux host, and PowerShell exact-file entry on actual 5.1 and supported 7, after their launch owners’ controls pass. Parser-only, helper-only, source inventory and whole-entry/native results must be labeled separately. A native host unavailable to the executor remains a qualification gap. Do not “test dry-run” by running the uncorrected full script against a live home directory.

## Alternatives, dependencies and closure

Keeping network allowed would make previews depend on rate limits, auth and current release content while still resolving no installed effect; the existing contract can be deterministic without it. Guarding only download misses eager mkdir, cache extraction and clipboard. An early return alone is fragile under later helper reuse, whereas a small entry plan plus local effect guards closes the current branches without a new command framework. Renaming the switch “mostly preview” evades the requested no-effect boundary. Disabling all operations unconditionally produces a false GREEN unless the normal positive control still reaches intended effects.

Preserve the accepted dependencies: [R0013](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/19) and [R0014](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/20) are qualification prerequisites for claimed native whole-entry results; [R0015](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/21) is the staging/lifetime interface. Analysis and bounded fixtures may proceed before those issues close. Keep one shared installer writer; no additional whole-issue serialization, issue merge or platform framework is proposed.

IMPLEMENTAUDIT R001D requires both usage surfaces and README/builder text where preview is exposed to state the same offline/no-effect policy. Keep preset bytes, config encoding, 325×530 embed, geolocation permission and manual installation boundary. Rollback guards only together with withdrawal of their no-effect claim; never delete cached/manual assets to reset a failed test. Stop on any observed effect, incompatible staging interface, missing native entry qualification or inability to isolate the fixture.

DONE requires final-tree RED→GREEN, complete branch/effect and normal-positive controls, exact native host evidence claimed, independent exact-tree review of the integrated effects, and an evidence comment before manual closure. Distribution claims additionally require authorized raw-script/usage readback on both platforms. Use non-closing `Implements #22` PR wording. Work-order publication and local helper results are not product, native-installation or deployed completion.

Methodology references (separate repository, not Salah work owners): [R001D in IMPLEMENTAUDIT](https://github.com/theislampill/IMPLEMENTAUDIT.md/issues/155).

Identity provenance: first repository-local allocation batch; existing GitHub object order was used to assign distinct monotonic hex-4 IDs. Closed/held IDs are not reused. Issue number is not implementation priority.

title: R0015: Prevent Bash installer writes through an attacker-prepared staging tree
body:
<!-- salah-widget-audit-20260907:SW-021 -->
# R0015: Prevent Bash installer writes through an attacker-prepared staging tree

**Repository-local identity:** `R0015` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#21](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/21). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Campaign draft alias: SW-021. Product defect; proposed priority P1, retaining SEC-002’s bounded unintended-overwrite witness. The Bash installer must create and use privately owned paths for every staged write. It must also retain the unpacked extension directory after exit, because Chromium’s manual “Load unpacked” path depends on that directory continuing to exist.

This is a repair to staging ownership and artifact lifetime. It is not a remote-code-execution finding, a Windows security claim, or authority to run an installer against real user data.

## Re-anchor and preserve the actual boundary

Main `fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624` and candidate `9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb` had byte-identical `install.sh` in the retained witness: SHA256 `89d919e365846ec5e3b31a0ed4a41f95e3364659336c04ab1f066abcd1173e63`. The function extracted with LF text had SHA256 `e47e541250c0a6cd61840f0c82337507dd8a59703fd0e18c61ba3f7cd6efcde2`. Those bind historical copies; do not assume a future checkout or distributed file still matches.

```text
git --no-optional-locks rev-parse --show-toplevel
git --no-optional-locks remote get-url origin
git --no-optional-locks status --short --branch
git --no-optional-locks rev-parse HEAD
git --no-optional-locks diff fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624 HEAD -- install.sh README.md
```

Confirm the intended `theislampill/salah_widget` checkout and its guidance before editing. Preserve dirty/unrelated work. Stop and reconcile changed staging paths, write sites, cleanup or output return contracts. The candidate is comparison evidence, not a whole-branch adoption mandate.

Public owners: [predictable initialization](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/install.sh#L34-L37), [asset download/extraction/preset writes](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/install.sh#L282-L356), [manual extension and import consumers](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/install.sh#L359-L427), [terminal staged-path claim](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/install.sh#L494-L502), [README manual boundary](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/README.md#L62-L68), and [candidate installer](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/install.sh).

## Demonstrated incident and what remains unproved

The installer constructs `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/salah-widget-installer`, then `mkdir -p` accepts a preexisting tree. It writes a predictable `presets/salah-widget.tablissng.json` with `curl -o`; configured content is subsequently read and rewritten at the same pathname. Neither operation checks whether that path is a symlink or whether its ancestors belong to this invocation.

The saved fixture prepared that preset pathname as a symlink to its own `fixture-victim.txt`, initially `unchanged sentinel\n`. It supplied harmless local JSON `{"fixture":"harmless","input":"#local=1"}` and hash `lat=24.47&lon=39.61&method=4`. The exact initialization and `download_preset()` followed the link, returned success, and left the victim as `{"fixture":"harmless","input":"#lat=24.47&lon=39.61&method=4"}`. `link-is-symlink=true` remained true. Both source copies exited 0.

This was actual fixture-file mutation under WSL Ubuntu on DrvFS, using local `file://` curl semantics. It did not involve a second UID, native Linux permission enforcement, native macOS, default `/tmp`, an actual browser profile, network access or a full wizard. The primitive is an installer-user-writable file overwrite. Cross-user exploitation depends on who can prepare/control the parent tree and when the installer uses it. Do not promote this evidence into arbitrary privileged overwrite, remote execution or a claim about PowerShell’s TEMP.

## Reproduce the RED safely from public inputs

Save this as `red-staging.py` in an authorized disposable directory. On a symlink-capable Linux/macOS fixture host, run `python3 red-staging.py /absolute/pinned/install.sh /absolute/authorized-fixture-parent`. It creates a new child under that parent, leaves it for inspection, and never executes the full wizard. Inspect the pinned source/extraction boundaries first; do not feed unknown installer text into this fixture.

```python
import hashlib, pathlib, subprocess, sys, tempfile
src = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding='utf-8')
parent = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2]).resolve(strict=True)
if not parent.is_dir(): raise SystemExit('fixture parent must exist')
root = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='staging-red-', dir=str(parent)))
victim = root / 'fixture-victim.txt'
victim.write_bytes(b'unchanged sentinel\n')
data = root / 'download.json'
data.write_bytes(b'{"fixture":"harmless","input":"#local=1"}\n')
presets = root / 'salah-widget-installer' / 'presets'
presets.mkdir(parents=True)
link = presets / 'salah-widget.tablissng.json'
link.symlink_to(victim)
before = hashlib.sha256(victim.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
init = src[src.index('WORK_ROOT='):src.index('\nsay_section()')]
fn = src[src.index('download_preset() {'):src.index('\ninstall_tablissng() {')]
program = r'''set -Eeuo pipefail
TMPDIR="$1"
SALAH_WIDGET_PRESET_URL="file://$1/download.json"
SALAH_WIDGET_HASH='lat=24.47&lon=39.61&method=4'
DRY_RUN=0
ok(){ printf '[OK] %s\n' "$1" >&2; }
warn(){ printf '[WARN] %s\n' "$1" >&2; }
''' + init + '\n' + fn + '\ndownload_preset\n'
r = subprocess.run(['bash','--noprofile','--norc','-c',program,'fixture',str(root)],
                   text=True,capture_output=True)
print('fixture', root, 'exit', r.returncode)
print('stdout', r.stdout, 'stderr', r.stderr)
print('before', before, 'after', hashlib.sha256(victim.read_bytes()).hexdigest())
print('symlink', link.is_symlink(), 'victim', victim.read_text())
```

The pinned RED must show changed victim bytes, the replacement hash in JSON, and a still-existing symlink. The GREEN oracle is byte-identical sentinel with normal output successfully written elsewhere in the newly owned tree; rejecting the hostile old tree is also safe if no output was promised. This fixture is a historical-mechanism reproduction recipe, not a newly executed PASS. The repaired entry and all write consumers need separate integration controls below.

## Selected repair: fresh private ownership, explicit retention

**1. Establish ownership before the first effect.** Move eager initialization out of top level into a small staging initializer called only after platform/input/eligible-target checks and only in non-dry execution. Use `umask 077` and the host’s established `mktemp -d` facility. Fail closed on creation/check failure; never fall back to the old predictable shared tree. Initialize path variables as unset/empty and record ownership only after successful creation and verification, so failure cleanup cannot accidentally interpret an empty variable as a parent/root target.

Use two directories with different lifetimes: a fresh transient download root under the validated temporary parent, and a fresh retained bundle directly under the validated user home, for example the proposed template `$HOME/salah-widget-install.XXXXXXXX`. Keeping the retained bundle under the user’s home avoids the OS purging the only unpacked extension from a temporary directory. Place the preset, Firefox installation file and final Chromium unpacked directory in the retained bundle. ZIP acquisition and incomplete downloads can stay transient. The exact generated bundle path is printed and copied only after its contents pass validation.

**2. Guard parents and children, not just the final leaf.** On the platform already selected by the script, use the native `stat` form (GNU `stat -c` on Linux, BSD `stat -f` on macOS), `id -u`, Bash `-O` and `-L`, and physical `pwd -P` checks. Qualify their actual availability on the claimed hosts; no `realpath -m` or newer Bash dependency is assumed. Resolve and verify the retained home parent: it must be owned by the current UID, a directory, and not writable by group/other. Reject a symlink in the supplied ownership boundary or an untrusted writable ancestor that could rename that boundary. A temporary parent may instead be root-owned sticky `/tmp`; a custom TMPDIR must satisfy a documented trusted-parent rule, not just be nonempty. If those checks cannot establish ownership on an unusual mount, stop with a manual path explanation rather than weakening them.

The new roots must resolve to their freshly created paths, belong to the current UID and have mode 0700. Existing retained bundles and the old shared cache are not silently reused. Derive children only from fixed names or existing sanitized leaf names, reject empty/`.`/`..` components and separators, and verify an output’s physical parent is inside the recorded root before each write, extraction or cleanup. Use a path-component boundary, so `/safe/root-other` does not count as inside `/safe/root`. Reject any preexisting symlink/nonregular output and symlinked directory component before proceeding. An attacker with the same UID is outside what these checks can isolate; do not claim this is a substitute for OS privilege separation.

**3. Keep the write chain closed.** Route `download_preset`, `download_tablissng_asset` and `expand_chromium_asset` through those owned roots. Download to a fresh file in an owned directory, validate, then make the final artifact available to the caller. Preserve exact `SALAH_WIDGET_HASH` substitution and JSON parsing behavior; do not follow a caller-supplied path into arbitrary storage. For extraction, use a new empty child instead of `rm -rf` on a derived preexisting unpacked directory. Validate archive member paths for absolute paths/parent traversal and disallow links escaping the extraction root using the available extraction tool’s supported behavior; if the tool cannot provide that check, stop rather than calling a successful unzip confinement proof. This is the direct all-write consumer check for the staging invariant, not a new signing or update framework.

**4. Make the artifact lifetime honest.** The retained bundle survives normal exit, errors after staging, and restart. Print “keep this directory while the unpacked extension is installed” for Chromium. Preset/XPI removal is manual after import/install and optional; the script must not guess that pressing Enter means the browser no longer needs a file. Never put the retained bundle in an unconditional EXIT trap. Transient cleanup may remove only this invocation’s verified owned scratch root; if identity changed or the path is a link, leave it and report the exact partial state. Retaining an incomplete owned bundle with an explicit failure label is safer than deleting a directory a user may already have loaded.

No migration of old predictable caches is included. Cross-run reuse of that unverified state is retired. **Same-attempt cache contract:** initialize one verified `DOWNLOAD_ROOT` for the current installer attempt; repeated selection of the same artifact within that attempt finds the regular owned file already downloaded there, returns the same path and avoids another asset fetch. Do not allocate a new root on each helper call, since that would defeat legitimate within-attempt reuse. **Cross-run contract:** the next invocation creates a different private root and never treats a prior shared cache or retained manual bundle as a silently admitted download cache. User-facing retained bundles remain available for their documented lifetime. This is the concrete private-cache interface consumed by the neighboring stdout/path owner and finalized for parent JOIN below.

## Why the tempting smaller fixes are insufficient

`chmod 700` on an existing predictable path can follow or legitimize attacker-prepared state; it does not establish fresh ownership. Checking only `-L "$dest"` leaves symlinked ancestors. A unique temporary root plus unconditional cleanup prevents this overwrite but destroys the manual unpacked-install path on exit. Leaving all artifacts under `/tmp` documents a lifetime that the installer cannot preserve across system cleanup. Reusing old shared downloads “for convenience” reintroduces the trust boundary the repair removed.

The chosen design adds one bounded staging initializer and a confinement check with real callers at each write/cleanup site. It reuses shell tools already needed by this installer family. It does not create a global cache database, background cleaner, per-user service, manifest protocol or signature authority. If more elaborate archive authentication is requested, stop and obtain a separate owner decision rather than claiming it from safe staging.

## Final-tree matrix and native limits

| Case | GREEN oracle / negative control |
|---|---|
| Exact hostile old preset symlink vector | Victim hash unchanged; old symlink untouched; valid output lives only in a new owned bundle. |
| Parent symlink, wrong UID, group/world-writable retained parent, symlink output, `..` or prefix-lookalike path | Fail before writing/extracting/deleting the target. Own sentinels outside the new root remain byte-identical. |
| Ordinary local preset with configured hash | Valid JSON has exact configured `#lat=24.47&lon=39.61&method=4`; returned path is one regular file in the retained bundle. |
| ZIP with nested manifest; malformed ZIP; traversal/symlink member | Valid confined extraction returns an existing in-root manifest directory; unsafe input fails and cannot change an outside sentinel. |
| Two invocations; same valid asset twice within one invocation | Distinct roots across runs; no implicit old-cache adoption; within-run reuse returns the same owned path without duplicate asset fetch. |
| Exit after download, preset failure, extraction failure, interrupt | Scratch cleanup only when ownership still matches; retained/manual directory remains usable or explicitly partial; no broad deletion. |
| Complete manual bundle then script exits | In an authorized disposable consumer, returned unpacked directory and manifest still exist after exit and restart; no automatic retention claim from a printed pathname alone. |
| DRY_RUN=1 after integration | No creation, permission change, copy, download, extraction or cleanup in either root; preview prints placeholders, not existing-artifact claims. |
| Mutants: restore predictable root; follow link; delete retained bundle at EXIT | Respectively victim/confinement/lifetime controls fail. |

Run filesystem probes only beneath explicit disposable fixture parents. For the cross-user claim, use native Linux with distinct fixture UIDs and native permission semantics, and qualify intended macOS/Bash behavior separately. WSL/DrvFS is retained primitive evidence, not the final native permission gate. Real browser loading requires separate authorization and disposable profiles; if not performed, label retained-path checks as filesystem lifetime proof only.

## Interfaces, rollback and closure

[R0016](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/22) has the accepted interface dependency on this owner and shares staging/preset/unpacked lifetimes; agree that initializer and cleanup are unreachable in dry-run. [R0013](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/19) owns stdout path bytes and same-attempt cached-path consumers. **Private-cache interface finalized for parent JOIN:** this owner supplies the newly created, verified root once per attempt and rejects automatic cross-run admission; the path owner proves first/second-call byte identity, stderr diagnostics and zero repeat asset fetch within that same root. Path creation/lifetime inside `download_tablissng_asset` is the shared hunk; stdout format remains with the path owner. The parent will reconcile SW-021→SW-019 and that collision in graph/pair/partition metadata. This body does not silently rewrite the accepted 25 edges or 496 pair dispositions, and the interface does not require waiting for the whole upstream issue to close. Shared installer writes and README lifetime text need one integrator.

IMPLEMENTAUDIT R001D applies to the real retained-path instructions, script usage and README. Preserve manual import, dashboard replacement warning, preset 325×530 dimensions/geolocation scope, encoded configuration and Bash 3.2. PowerShell staging is outside this witness. Rollback may move to another verified private path or retain safe bundles; it must never restore writes through the predictable shared tree. Never recursively delete an unverified old path or preexisting user artifact during migration or rollback.

DONE requires the final integrated tree’s sentinel, ownership, confinement, lifetime and dry-run controls, the actual native-host evidence claimed, independent exact-tree security review, and an evidence comment recording exact commit, fixture inputs/results and remaining mount/host limitations. Any public installer claim additionally needs authorized distributed-byte/instruction readback. Use non-closing `Implements #21` PR wording and manual closure after evidence. Publishing the work order establishes neither a repaired installer nor a successful extension installation.

Methodology references (separate repository, not Salah work owners): [R001D in IMPLEMENTAUDIT](https://github.com/theislampill/IMPLEMENTAUDIT.md/issues/155).

Identity provenance: first repository-local allocation batch; existing GitHub object order was used to assign distinct monotonic hex-4 IDs. Closed/held IDs are not reused. Issue number is not implementation priority.

title: R0014: Repair PowerShell minimum-host parsing and release-asset selection
body:
<!-- salah-widget-audit-20260907:SW-020 -->
# R0014: Repair PowerShell minimum-host parsing and release-asset selection

**Repository-local identity:** `R0014` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#20](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/20). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Campaign draft alias: SW-020. Product defect; proposed priority P1. The exact downloaded file must parse on declared Windows PowerShell 5.1, and valid release assets must reach the manual-install path. VAL-005 establishes a file-decoding failure before execution; VAL-004 independently establishes a selector failure after parsing. Repair both. A newer host or successful store fallback can hide one failure without fixing it.

## Baseline and evidence custody

Historical source: main `fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624`, candidate `9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb`. Both produced the same selector exception. Before future edits, bind the authorized checkout and preserve unrelated work:

```text
git --no-optional-locks rev-parse --show-toplevel
git --no-optional-locks remote get-url origin
git --no-optional-locks status --short --branch
git --no-optional-locks rev-parse HEAD
git --no-optional-locks diff fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624 HEAD -- install.ps1 README.md builder.html
```

Require the intended `theislampill/salah_widget` target and inspect any changed encoding, selector, callers and advertised host. Stop on incompatible drift; do not assume the old defect survives at a future HEAD. The candidate is not approved for wholesale adoption.

Owners are [install.ps1 exact file/minimum-host declaration](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/install.ps1#L1-L26), [Select-TablissNgAsset](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/install.ps1#L314-L339), [download/manual/fallback consumers](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/install.ps1#L341-L503), [the non-ASCII display string](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/install.ps1#L527-L535), [README Windows route](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/README.md#L41-L68) and [builder Windows command](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/builder.html#L344-L357). [Candidate installer](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/install.ps1) is comparison evidence.

## What actually failed, and competing interpretations

The 7 September controlled native-host probe recorded Windows PowerShell `5.1.26100.9168` and PowerShell `7.6.5`. On 5.1, `Parser.ParseFile` over the BOM-less UTF-8 file returned four errors, at source lines 535, 535, 583 and 527: unexpected `{`, missing `)`, missing string terminator, missing `}`. Its initial bytes were `35,32,83`, not a UTF-8 BOM. Explicit UTF-8 `ReadAllText` followed by `ParseInput` returned zero errors; PS7 `ParseFile` also returned zero. This differential ties the failure to exact file decoding. It does not establish that README’s `irm | iex` response-string route fails identically, and it does not make a PS7-only parse an acceptable 5.1 gate.

The independently extracted selector was given `tabliss-chromium.zip` and `tabliss-firefox-signed.xpi` as in-memory release assets. On both hosts and both source trees it threw `Cannot convert 'System.Object[]' to the type 'System.String' required by parameter 'Property'. Specified method is not supported.` The comma after each `Where-Object` pipeline inside `@(...)` changes argument binding; this is not a missing upstream release or failed download. `Install-TablissNG` catches the exception and offers a store, so observing a store prompt would not prove valid GitHub selection.

No whole wizard, download, store opening, browser profile mutation or extension installation was executed by this evidence. Four independent combinations of tree/family share the same implementation and are not four independent defect mechanisms.

## Public RED recipe: exact bytes plus bounded selector

Save this as `red-powershell.ps1` outside the source checkout. Execute it with both actual hosts, supplying an absolute source file path:

```powershell
powershell.exe -NoProfile -File .\red-powershell.ps1 -SourceFile C:\fixture\install.ps1
pwsh.exe -NoProfile -File .\red-powershell.ps1 -SourceFile C:\fixture\install.ps1
```

The fixture does not execute installer top level or call a remote API. Its text is ASCII-safe so the fixture itself does not reproduce the decoding mistake accidentally.

```powershell
param([Parameter(Mandatory=$true)][string]$SourceFile)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$tokens=$null; $fileErrors=$null
$null=[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile(
  $SourceFile,[ref]$tokens,[ref]$fileErrors)
$text=[IO.File]::ReadAllText($SourceFile,[Text.Encoding]::UTF8)
$tokens=$null; $textErrors=$null
$ast=[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseInput(
  $text,[ref]$tokens,[ref]$textErrors)
if (@($textErrors).Count) { throw 'Unexpected source syntax drift' }
$defs=@($ast.FindAll({param($n)
  $n -is [System.Management.Automation.Language.FunctionDefinitionAst] -and
  $n.Name -eq 'Select-TablissNgAsset'
},$true))
if ($defs.Count -ne 1) { throw 'Selector identity mismatch' }
. ([scriptblock]::Create($defs[0].Extent.Text))
function Get-LatestRelease {
  [pscustomobject]@{tag_name='fixture'; assets=@(
    [pscustomobject]@{name='tabliss-chromium.zip'; browser_download_url='https://example.invalid/chromium'}
    [pscustomobject]@{name='tabliss-firefox-signed.xpi'; browser_download_url='https://example.invalid/firefox'}
  )}
}
$rows=foreach($family in 'chromium','firefox') {
  try {
    $chosen=@(Select-TablissNgAsset $family)
    [pscustomobject]@{family=$family; result='selected'; count=$chosen.Count; names=@($chosen.name)}
  } catch {
    [pscustomobject]@{family=$family; result='threw'; error=$_.Exception.Message}
  }
}
[pscustomobject]@{
  host=$PSVersionTable.PSVersion.ToString()
  fileErrors=@($fileErrors).Count
  fileErrorLines=@($fileErrors | ForEach-Object {$_.Extent.StartLineNumber})
  explicitUtf8Errors=@($textErrors).Count
  cases=@($rows)
} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6
```

At the pinned RED baseline: 5.1 fileErrors=4, explicitUtf8Errors=0; PS7 both=0; both families throw the Property-binding error on both hosts. Extracting from explicit UTF-8 text is intentional isolation of the second defect, not a replacement for the exact-file parser gate. Run final GREEN against the repaired file and, when distribution is claimed, against bytes freshly read from the authorized raw-script endpoint. Never resave that downloaded copy through a text editor before hashing and parsing it.

## Staged implementation design

**1. Repair byte interpretation without raising the floor.** Keep `#requires -Version 5.1`. Prefer making the installer source ASCII-safe: replace the decorative em dash in the quoted status line with ` - `, inspect remaining non-ASCII bytes, and normalize only display/comment text needed for this policy. Preserve variable-expanded Unicode browser/profile paths and preset/config strings; source encoding policy does not mean transliterating user data. A byte scan of the final distributed script must find no byte above 127 if this option is selected. A UTF-8 BOM is a viable competing policy, but it relies on every distribution/rewrite step retaining that marker; choose it only with a byte-preservation gate. Raising the minimum to PS7 transfers avoidable installation work to users and evades the admitted 5.1 contract.

Intermediate acceptance: final file parses on both native hosts before any whole-entry fixture is credited. Keep the pre-repair bytes as the RED discriminator. `ParseInput` remains an explanation control, never the sole acceptance gate.

**2. Repair ordering at the existing selector.** Remove pipeline-separating commas and emit each candidate pipeline as a separate statement inside `@(...)`, or concatenate separately parenthesized arrays. Prefer the former: each complete pipeline contributes zero or more objects in stable order without additional state. Keep `Select-Object -First 1` and exactly one returned object after flattening; diagnostics go through `Write-Host`/warning channels, not the success pipeline. Preserve existing source order within each preference tier.

The retained tier contract is precise:

| Family | Tier precedence | Exclusions |
|---|---|---|
| Chromium | ZIP name matching `chrom(e|ium)`, then a `tabliss*.zip` fallback | Names containing firefox, safari or source |
| Firefox | XPI with signed/firefox in name, then other XPI, then firefox ZIP fallback | Names containing unsigned or source |

These are filename filters. They neither verify a signature nor prove the fallback Firefox ZIP is installable through “Install Add-on From File”. The earlier phrase “signed Firefox requirements” must not become a new cryptographic claim. Retain rejection of explicitly unsigned/source builds and the current preference semantics in this repair. If the owner wants to prohibit generic XPI or ZIP fallback, that needs a separately stated compatibility/security decision; do not silently change those tiers while fixing syntax.

**3. Qualify the consumer without letting catch hide failure.** Invoke `Install-TablissNG` in an effect-stubbed fixture after parsing succeeds. With the valid release fixture, assert `Download-Asset` receives exactly the selected object; Chromium reaches `Expand-ChromiumAsset` with the returned path and Firefox reaches its existing manual path. Replace `Open-TargetUrl`, `Copy-Text`, `Read-Host`, downloads and extraction with in-memory spies. Record which branch ran. Valid assets must never hit the “Falling back” path. Empty/no-match releases may reach fallback, with an honest unavailable diagnostic. Unsupported family remains an error. A network/auth failure remains a network/auth failure, not “installed”.

**4. Update distribution-facing claims as a unit.** Keep the README’s response-string route and the script’s review/download/`-File` route accurate, including the exact supported host and manual action boundary. Change builder Windows command only if its actual invocation changes; do not churn the encoded hash grammar or preset content. IMPLEMENTAUDIT R001D applies to exact distributed bytes and usage prose, not merely a local syntax result. IMPLEMENTAUDIT R001E applies to the native parser fixture and actual selector caller, preventing unused test helpers from standing in for entry qualification.

## Deterministic GREEN and mutation controls

| Fixture | Required result |
|---|---|
| Exact final file on PS5.1 and PS7 | Zero ParseFile errors; explicit UTF-8 control also zero; record host version, file SHA256 and encoding policy. |
| Valid Chromium ZIP + signed Firefox XPI | One object per family with the exact appropriate name and URL; no fallback. |
| Put `tabliss.zip` before `tabliss-chromium.zip` in source array | Chromium-specific tier still wins despite array order. Reverse within one tier to verify stable source order. |
| `source.zip`, `tabliss-firefox-unsigned.xpi`, `safari.zip`, competing family | These never displace a valid same-family asset. Only unsuitable assets produces the existing no-safe-asset error. |
| Empty assets; unsupported `safari`; metadata exception | Defined rejection; stubbed manual store fallback only where the actual caller owns it. No download/open occurs accidentally. |
| Generic XPI / Firefox ZIP only | Explicitly characterize retained fallback selection; do not label signature authenticity or browser installability PASS. |
| Paths/config containing spaces and Unicode | Caller receives unchanged strings, despite ASCII-safe script source. |
| Reinsert comma; restore original BOM-less non-ASCII bytes | Selector and native file gate respectively fail. Neither PS7 parsing nor catch/store success can mask those mutants. |

Whole-file `-File` entry proof needs a disposable, fully effect-stubbed/native environment. Its setup must intercept `New-Item`, profile discovery, web requests, clipboard, process launch, extraction and deletion before top-level execution; do not launch the current installer against the owner’s profiles merely to show that parsing works. Host unavailability is an open native qualification gap, not a skipped PASS.

## Siblings, rollback and DONE

No hard whole-issue predecessor is introduced. [R0016](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/22) already consumes this work’s qualification contract for Windows no-effect preview. Agree the source owner for final `install.ps1` integration: its effect guards must not reintroduce a non-ASCII parsing problem or alter selector output, and this issue must not absorb its dry-run work. [R0013](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/19) owns Bash. Shared README/test insertions use the designated integrator. No new edge or broad platform campaign is needed.

Preserve manual extension installation, explicit dashboard-replacement warning, builder config carry-through, the preset’s 325×530 iframe and permission scope. Roll back the bounded encoding/selector patch and matching tests if a supported artifact path regresses, but remove any unsupported host claim at the same time. Keep actual downloaded/manual assets; no cleanup or profile rollback belongs to this authoring issue. Stop on incompatible drift, absent minimum-host qualification, broken selector controls or unresolved Firefox policy changes.

DONE requires final-tree RED→GREEN/control evidence on both claimed hosts, exact-byte identity, consumer branch proof, and an evidence comment before manual closure. Where publication/distribution is claimed, additionally bind the authorized raw-script readback to those bytes; a local fix does not prove public replacement. Use non-closing `Implements #20` PR wording. A work-order publication, parser success, selected asset, downloaded file and installed extension remain distinct outcomes.

Methodology references (separate repository, not Salah work owners): [R001D in IMPLEMENTAUDIT](https://github.com/theislampill/IMPLEMENTAUDIT.md/issues/155), [R001E in IMPLEMENTAUDIT](https://github.com/theislampill/IMPLEMENTAUDIT.md/issues/157).

Identity provenance: first repository-local allocation batch; existing GitHub object order was used to assign distinct monotonic hex-4 IDs. Closed/held IDs are not reused. Issue number is not implementation priority.

title: R0013: Repair Bash installer input, supported-shell and cached-path contracts
body:
<!-- salah-widget-audit-20260907:SW-019 -->
# R0013: Repair Bash installer input, supported-shell and cached-path contracts

**Repository-local identity:** `R0013` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#19](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/19). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Campaign draft alias: SW-019. Product defect; proposed priority P1. This work order retains three accepted failures, VAL-003/006/007, under one existing Bash launch owner. It authorizes no implementation or external effect.

The advertised command must obtain answers from the person at the terminal, detect targets on the claimed Bash floor, and deliver one actual asset path to its caller. Today’s pinned evidence shows three breaks in that chain: script bytes become the menu answer, macOS detection requires an unavailable builtin, and cached download status contaminates the returned path. A successful helper exit or a printed “Done” did not establish installation.

## Bind the repair before editing

The evidence baseline is main `fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624`; candidate `9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb` reproduced the same cases. The candidate is not a branch-adoption instruction. In the explicitly authorized future checkout run:

```text
git --no-optional-locks rev-parse --show-toplevel
git --no-optional-locks remote get-url origin
git --no-optional-locks status --short --branch
git --no-optional-locks rev-parse HEAD
git --no-optional-locks diff fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624 HEAD -- install.sh builder.html README.md
```

Confirm the `theislampill/salah_widget` target, read closer guidance, and preserve unrelated dirty work. Inspect relevant differences before using the pinned extraction ranges below. Stop if stdin handling, staging return types, target encoding or the generated command changed incompatibly; adapt the fixture to the actual named functions rather than attributing an old defect to arbitrary HEAD.

Exact owners: [install.sh initialization, output and detection](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/install.sh#L16-L246), [download and install callers](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/install.sh#L282-L427), [selection and terminal text](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/install.sh#L446-L502), [builder installCmd](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/builder.html#L344-L357), and [README invocation/manual boundary](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/README.md#L41-L68). [Candidate installer](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/install.sh) is a comparison source only.

## Incident, causal chain and limits

1. README and `installCmd()` send downloaded program text through `bash` stdin. The line-464 `read` uses that same stream. In the saved controlled-source run it consumed the following assignment, producing `selection=<selection="${selection:-all}">`, exit 0. Running the identical excerpt through `bash -c` with `all\n` on stdin produced `selection=<all>`. An unrecognized selection matches no target at lines 474–477; the loop can finish and still print “Downloads and presets were staged”. The source also has four later interactive reads at 364/372/381/404, so fixing only the initial menu leaves the same ownership error downstream.
2. Darwin is admitted at line 55, but both profile branches call `mapfile`. The retained [Apple Bash 3.2 builtin source](https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/bash/blob/51bf3fc6f26e9517c3a2e4bc3d208f9b39b87178/bash-3.2/builtins/Makefile.in) lacks it. The actual detector with inert profile helpers printed `detected` on Git Bash 5.3.9; disabling only `mapfile` exited 127. This identifies a required capability. It is not a native macOS installation or a complete emulation of Bash 3.2.
3. `download_tablissng_asset` checks its cached file, calls `ok`, prints the path and returns 0. `ok` writes stdout. The caller captures both lines through `path="$(...)"`; extraction and Firefox clipboard instructions consume that polluted value. The saved result was `<[OK] Already downloaded tabliss-chromium.zip\n/fixture/v1/tabliss-chromium.zip>`. No full installer, remote asset, browser or profile was exercised.

These are independent causal subcases. The good builder serializer, fixed 325×530 iframe and manual import boundary are retained controls, not evidence against the launch defects. URL encoding already kept quote/newline/command-substitution text inert; preserve it.

## Public RED fixture, without the private audit harness

Save the following as `red-bash.cjs` in a disposable fixture directory and run `node red-bash.cjs /absolute/path/to/the/pinned/install.sh`. It reads the source but executes only the named excerpts with inert effects; it never invokes installer top level. `BASH_EXE` may name the host Bash executable. Use the pinned source for the fixed ranges.

```js
const fs = require('fs'), cp = require('child_process');
const src = fs.readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8').split(/\r?\n/);
const exact = (a,b) => src.slice(a-1,b).join('\n');
const bash = process.env.BASH_EXE || 'bash';
const run = (input,args=[]) => {
  const r=cp.spawnSync(bash,['--noprofile','--norc',...args],{input,encoding:'utf8'});
  return {exit:r.status,stdout:r.stdout,stderr:r.stderr};
};
const menu='set -Eeuo pipefail\n'+exact(464,465)+'\nprintf "selection=<%s>\\n" "$selection"\n';
console.log('source-on-stdin',run(menu));
console.log('answer-on-stdin',run('all\n',['-c',menu]));
const detector='set -Eeuo pipefail\n'+exact(215,246)+`
CONFIGS=("c|Chrome|chromium|fixture|chrome|new|old|store|manager|newtab")
find_exe(){ printf chrome; }
chromium_profiles(){ printf fixture; }
has_id_dir(){ return 1; }
add_target(){ printf 'detected\\n'; }
`;
console.log('builtin-present',run(detector+'detect_targets\n'));
console.log('builtin-disabled',run(detector+'enable -n mapfile\ndetect_targets\n'));
console.log('cache',run('set -Eeuo pipefail\n'+exact(40,40)+'\n'+exact(112,114)+'\n'+exact(282,304)+`
DOWNLOAD_ROOT=/fixture
DRY_RUN=0
select_asset(){ printf 'v1\\ttabliss-chromium.zip\\thttps://example.invalid/file\\n'; }
mkdir(){ :; }
curl(){ printf 'unexpected-network' >&2; return 99; }
[(){ if test "$1" = -f; then return 0; else builtin [ "$@"; fi; }
path="$(download_tablissng_asset chromium)"
printf 'captured=<%s>\\n' "$path"
`));
```

The RED oracles are the three exact outcomes above, with the `-c` and builtin-present positives. Keep the archived outputs as historical, not a new execution report. For GREEN use symbol-bounded extraction after range changes and separately exercise the real entry path; a fixture that only tests a new helper while old reads remain reachable cannot qualify this issue.

## Ordered repair and executable contracts

**A. Give interactive input one owner.** Preserve the pipe command by opening a dedicated readable controlling-terminal descriptor once, before staging or prompts. Use a fixed descriptor such as 3 for Bash 3.2 compatibility (`exec 3</dev/tty`, checked); route every human `read` through `-u 3`. Keep structured record reads (`IFS='|' read`, here-strings, release TSV) on their explicit data input. Print prompts on stderr. On unavailable terminal or EOF, emit an error and exit nonzero before installation effects; do not turn EOF into the default answer. A successful empty terminal line may retain default `all`/source 1. Close the descriptor at exit without interfering with the staging owner's cleanup.

This makes a tiny input helper warranted: the menu, source choice and three confirmation branches must all call it. It must return failure to the caller; callers may not swallow it and continue. Do not let it write answers to stdout where a path-returning caller could capture them. `read -r -u 3 variable` in the caller, or a helper using Bash `read`'s caller-scope variable behavior with distinct local names, is sufficient; no new CLI parser or dependency is needed.

**B. Validate target intent before effects.** Normalize whitespace, admit only `all` or comma-separated existing indices, reject a malformed/out-of-range token with a named diagnostic, and deduplicate valid repeated indices. Compute the selected set before downloads. Preserve the legacy-Tabliss skip rule. An empty detection set, invalid selection, EOF, or an all-legacy selection cannot claim staged completion. Track eligible targets and whether a preset/asset was actually produced; terminal text distinguishes “no eligible target”, “manual action pending”, and “files staged”. Pressing Enter is acknowledgment, not independent proof of extension installation.

**C. Replace both `mapfile` calls locally.** Reset `profiles=()` for each browser config, then use `while IFS= read -r p || [ -n "$p" ]; do profiles+=("$p"); done < <(chromium_profiles "$user_data")`, with the corresponding Firefox producer. The redirection keeps the loop in the current shell; `producer | while ...` would lose the populated array in a subshell. Retain the zero-profile fallback when an executable or user-data directory exists. Check native Bash 3.2 empty-array behavior under `set -u`, using a guarded iteration if necessary; do not globally relax `nounset`. Paths with spaces/Unicode/backslashes are single entries. The existing newline-delimited profile format cannot represent newline-bearing paths; disclose that retained limitation instead of claiming arbitrary-byte path support or replacing the whole target record format.

**D. Preserve the value/status boundary.** Make `ok` write stderr, then inspect actual command-substitution consumers (`find_exe`, `select_asset`, `download_tablissng_asset`, `expand_chromium_asset`, `download_preset`) for stray status output. Success from the download helper means stdout is exactly one newline-terminated absolute existing file path; failure is nonzero with no usable path. Cached and fresh calls return the same bytes. Retain quoting in extraction/copy/open callers. Cache policy and ownership remain with [R0015](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/21); this issue proves reuse of a valid owned cache entry, not trust in an old shared path.

**E. Integrate the generated command and actual entry.** Retain `URLSearchParams` serialization in `hash()` and `SALAH_WIDGET_HASH='encoded-value'` at the Bash process. README and builder should explain a terminal is required and retain review/download/file invocation. The visible command can remain `curl ... | bash` after input separation; qualify that exact shape under a pseudo-terminal with local script bytes and effect stubs. A file-only documentation workaround is a legitimate smaller fallback only if both public generators change and the old route fails clearly; it leaves copied historical pipe commands broken, so it is not the preferred repair.

## GREEN, controls and mutation matrix

| Case | Expected final behavior / discriminating control |
|---|---|
| Pipe + real PTY; answers `all`, `1,3`, empty line | Select the actual eligible set; all subsequent prompts read only PTY bytes. Effect stubs log expected selected targets. |
| No controlling terminal, EOF, `999`, `1,bad`, no targets | Nonzero, explicit reason, no staging/open/copy; no “files staged” success. |
| Targets 1/2/3; answer `1,1,3`; target 3 legacy | Target 1 reached once; target 3 explicitly refused; no legacy profile write. |
| Both browser families; zero/one/multiple profiles, `/fixture/Profile One`, `/fixture/مدينة`, trailing line without newline | Stable cardinality and exact path values on native Apple Bash 3.2 and modern Bash; empty-array nounset boundary included. |
| Fresh vs valid owned cached ZIP/XPI | Single existing path on stdout, diagnostics only stderr; cache hit makes zero asset fetches; extraction/copy receives byte-identical path. |
| Malicious label literal `a'"&\u0060$(x)\n<z>` through builder | Percent-encoded shell value and exact decode roundtrip; local mode omits coordinates; iframe remains 325×530 with original permission scope. |
| Mutants: restore one stdin read; restore `mapfile`; send cache status to stdout | Corresponding entry/host/path control fails separately. This prevents one corrected subcase masking two remaining failures. |

Use in-memory/effect-stubbed controls first. Native macOS evidence must come from actual `/bin/bash --version` plus detector and terminal entry execution on that host; disabling a builtin in a modern shell is insufficient. Do not open real profiles, install extensions or contact a live release in these controls.

## Integration, public effects and closure

[R0014](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/20) owns Windows parsing/selection. [R0015](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/21) owns safe staging and retention. [R0016](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/22) has the accepted qualification dependency on this launch contract and shares `bash/download-return`; its dry-run must not return a pretend existing path to extraction. Agree these interfaces before merging shared installer hunks, with one installer writer.

**Private-cache interface finalized for parent JOIN:** [R0015](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/21) supplies one newly created, verified private download root for an installer attempt. This owner calls `download_tablissng_asset` twice for the same selected fixture asset within that attempt: the first call creates the regular file, the second recognizes that same owned file, returns byte-identical single-path stdout and makes zero further asset downloads. Neither this test nor the helper adopts an earlier invocation’s predictable/shared path. A later invocation gets a different private root; the security owner deliberately retires automatic cross-run reuse of old shared caches and retains any user-facing manual bundle without treating it as a trusted new download cache. Thus same-attempt cache output/reuse is this owner’s invariant, while cross-run root admission/lifetime is the staging owner’s invariant. Disclose that compatibility behavior in README and integrated evidence. The parent owns the corresponding SW-021→SW-019 interface edge and exact path-creation hunk reconciliation; this text creates no independent graph mutation or whole-issue prerequisite. Shared docs/test insertion uses the designated integrator, not competing README rewrites.

IMPLEMENTAUDIT R001D applies to script, builder command and README as one public capability. Preserve preset configuration carry-through, 325×530 layout, geolocation permission, manual import and dashboard replacement warning. No auto-install, package-manager prerequisite, staging security redesign, or whole candidate adoption belongs here. Retaining Bash 3.2 via two loops is smaller than requiring Homebrew/new Bash; changing all stdout to a machine protocol or rewriting the installer would add unrelated compatibility risks.

Rollback each subcase with its matching command/docs/tests. Never leave the public terminal/shell claim stronger than the reverted script, and never restore unsafe staging as a convenience rollback. On partial success retain exact staged paths and state manual actions remain pending; do not remove prior user artifacts. Stop on incompatible drift, failed native floor, malformed return bytes or an unresolved staging/preview interface.

DONE requires final-tree RED→GREEN and the listed negative/mutation controls, the minimum-host/real-entry evidence claimed, independent exact-tree review where installer integration warrants it, and an evidence comment binding commit, commands, host versions, results and remaining limits. Any distribution claim also needs authorized raw-script and generated-command readback; local tests do not prove deployed bytes. Use non-closing `Implements #19` PR wording, then manual closure after evidence. Publishing this work order repairs no installer.

Methodology references (separate repository, not Salah work owners): [R001D in IMPLEMENTAUDIT](https://github.com/theislampill/IMPLEMENTAUDIT.md/issues/155).

Identity provenance: first repository-local allocation batch; existing GitHub object order was used to assign distinct monotonic hex-4 IDs. Closed/held IDs are not reused. Issue number is not implementation priority.

title: R0012: Make copy success and manual recovery correspond to the requested payload
body:
<!-- salah-widget-audit-20260907:SW-018 -->
# R0012: Make copy success and manual recovery correspond to the requested payload

**Repository-local identity:** `R0012` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#18](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/18). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Campaign draft alias: SW-018. Product defect; proposed P2. This repair concerns copy outcome and recovery, not command execution or installer correctness.

## Historical witness and causal boundary

The 7 September 2026 original-source VM fixture rejected navigator.clipboard.writeText and made document.execCommand("copy") return false. On both main fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624 and candidate 9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb, Copy embed still displayed "copied ✓". Install widget instead displayed "Couldn’t copy — select the embed code box and copy manually." That box held an iframe, not the terminal command requested by Install.

The [embed handler](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/builder.html#L331) does not inspect fallback success and unconditionally sets success text. The [existing copyText and install handler](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/builder.html#L360) already return/use a boolean, but the install failure points at the wrong artifact. A successful primary clipboard write is the retained positive control. Hostile label encoding, platform selection and 325×530 iframe size passed separate bounded controls; no injection or malformed installer command is established here. The fixture never used the owner's clipboard, a live browser or a terminal installer.

The invariant is **a success message follows actual copy success, and manual recovery exposes the exact payload captured for that action**. A failed operation must not direct a user to a different artifact.

## Exact repair with the existing helper

Before authorized work, bind repository root, theislampill/salah_widget remote, HEAD and dirty paths; inspect relevant drift with:

~~~sh
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git remote get-url origin
git rev-parse HEAD
git status --short
git diff fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624 -- builder.html tests/smoke.html README.md
~~~

The write owner is builder.html copy onclick, copyText, install onclick and their status/recovery markup. [installCmd](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/builder.html#L344) remains a read/compatibility owner. The [candidate builder](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/builder.html) is not a prequalified patch.

1. Capture each payload once at button activation: current #code.value for Embed; installCmd().cmd for Install. Call the existing copyText(payload) from both handlers. Set success only for true; a rejected/false fallback is failure. Harden only helper cleanup needed for a thrown fallback: remove its temporary textarea and retain a boolean result without letting cleanup hide a failure.
2. Keep the embed-code box an embed-code box. On embed failure show "Couldn’t copy. Select the embed code below and copy it manually." Focus/select the exact captured payload in the recovery surface. On install failure show "Couldn’t copy. Select the install command below and copy it manually." Reveal a labeled readonly textarea adjacent to install feedback containing the captured command. Never write the command into the embed textarea or change command quoting.
3. Use one small manual-recovery surface for the install action; the existing embed textarea suffices when its current value still equals the captured iframe. If the form changes while a copy is pending, preserve the action's captured iframe in a labeled recovery textarea rather than silently selecting a newly generated iframe. A single shared recovery region labeled by artifact kind is an acceptable compact implementation; it must retain the payload/action association and must not replace the canonical embed output.
4. Associate async completion and timeout cleanup with that button's current copy attempt. Disable that button while its attempt is pending, restore it in cleanup, and clear its prior status timer before writing new feedback. Keep separate embed/install status ownership so an earlier success-reset timer cannot clear a newer failure. Do not auto-hide the manual payload after eight seconds: retain it until a new action of the same kind replaces it or the user dismisses it. Restore focus to the activating button on success; move focus/select to manual recovery on failure.

A local per-action attempt counter is sufficient where disabling cannot prevent programmatic reentry; do not add a global clipboard scheduler. This is action-result ownership, not the separate location-intent domain. New clipboard permissions, automatic permission prompts or a copy library do not repair false feedback. Removing fallback entirely would regress browsers where the existing boolean fallback works. Regenerating a command after await could select changed form values or platform state, violating recovery identity.

## Standalone fixture and exact expected payloads

Run future tests with a controlled clipboard/execCommand double in a disposable origin. Do not write the owner's real clipboard. The stimulus is:

~~~js
const written = [];
navigator.clipboard.writeText = async t => {
  written.push(t);
  throw new Error("controlled clipboard denial");
};
document.execCommand = command => {
  if (command !== "copy") throw new Error("unexpected command");
  return false;
};
// Activate the actual Embed or Install button.
// Assert no copied-success text, and recovery.value === written[0].
~~~

Where the browser property is read-only, install the equivalent configurable test double before application load. Do not change production permissions to make the test possible.

Use a builder fixture at https://example.test/widget/builder.html with portable label Madinah, latitude 24.4672, longitude 39.6142, method 4, school 0, time 24 and units f. The historical iframe src is https://example.test/widget/#lat=24.4672&lon=39.6142&label=Madinah&method=4&school=0. Capture the complete actual snippet, including newlines and 325×530 style; compare recovery byte-for-byte, not just "contains iframe".

For platform Win32, current installCmd yields:

~~~powershell
$env:SALAH_WIDGET_HASH='lat=24.4672&lon=39.6142&label=Madinah&method=4&school=0'; irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theislampill/salah_widget/main/install.ps1 | iex
~~~

For MacIntel/Linux, current command shape is:

~~~sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theislampill/salah_widget/main/install.sh | SALAH_WIDGET_HASH='lat=24.4672&lon=39.6142&label=Madinah&method=4&school=0' bash
~~~

These strings are **test data; do not execute them**. For intentional generic local=1, the current command omits SALAH_WIDGET_HASH. Qualify actual generated strings on the final tree; do not hardcode obsolete strings after an authorized serializer change.

| Copy path/control | Expected output |
|---|---|
| Primary resolves | Success; fallback call count 0; no manual-error message. |
| Primary rejects, fallback true | Success; captured payload was passed to both mechanisms. |
| Primary rejects, fallback false or throws | No copied/checkmark success; accessible failure and exact manual payload remain available. |
| Clipboard API absent | Controlled fallback follows the same true/false outcomes without an uncaught exception. |
| Embed vs Install; Windows vs Bash | Recovery kind/name and bytes match the requested artifact, never another button's output. |
| Form changes while pending; old status timer fires | Result remains bound to captured payload; newer failure is not cleared by old timer. |
| Label includes apostrophe, quotes, ampersand, newline, Unicode and command-substitution-looking literal text | Existing URLSearchParams encoding and exact decoded label survive; no raw quote breakout or command execution. |
| Mutation: unconditional success or install recovery wired to #code | Respective through-button assertion fails. |

The minimum browser bridge uses actual button activation, rejection doubles and native textarea focus/selection. Capture readable failure text and selected recovery, then keyboard Tab onward; test narrow/mobile width and a long command without page overflow. The VM cannot establish selection, focus or screen-reader announcements. Clipboard doubles cannot prove a real permission policy; report that boundary.

## Interfaces, public effects and DONE

No new typed dependency is proposed. [R0010](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/16) may change the carried local fragment; this work compares against the actual captured artifact. [R0013](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/19) and [R0014](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/20) own Bash/minimum-PowerShell installer execution. Correctly recovering their command is not proof it installs successfully. Serially join shared builder markup/docs through the existing integrator.

Keep generated payload grammar, 325×530 iframe, geolocation attribute scope, config.js, index.html, installer sources and preset unchanged. Add README recovery text only if it describes these buttons; no published copy-success claim until served builder bytes and UI are read back.

Rollback handler/recovery changes together if success paths or focus regress, preserving the canonical embed textarea. Stop on incompatible command grammar or absent browser selection evidence; retain pure-source results as partial. DONE needs final-tree RED→GREEN plus positive/mutation controls, browser feedback/selection evidence and an evidence comment. Use non-closing Implements #18 PR wording and manual closure after evidence and any claimed public readback. This proposal asserts no implementation PASS.

Identity provenance: first repository-local allocation batch; existing GitHub object order was used to assign distinct monotonic hex-4 IDs. Closed/held IDs are not reused. Issue number is not implementation priority.

title: R0011: Report settings save and reset outcomes from actual storage results
body:
<!-- salah-widget-audit-20260907:SW-017 -->
# R0011: Report settings save and reset outcomes from actual storage results

**Repository-local identity:** `R0011` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#17](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/17). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Campaign draft alias: SW-017. Product defect; proposed P2. Scope is the existing settings persistence contract; it is not an erasure feature or implementation authority.

## Observed outcome mismatch

On both main fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624 and unmerged candidate 9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb:

- With a saved London configuration and removeItem throwing a DOMException named SecurityError, _resetLocal immediately says "Local settings cleared." After controlled detection failure, it says "Local settings cleared — enter your location." The London record remains readable, and _storageErr is null.
- With setItem throwing SecurityError, changing units to c through _commitSettings still applies units c to the live CONFIG and sets _storageErr to SecurityError. The visible-status field remains "Enter to search a place · Shift+Enter to keep the typed name." Shared saveLocal already returned {ok:false,error:"SecurityError"}.
- README promises that the widget says when saving is unavailable. A separate source census found _storageErr declared, assigned, reset and exposed diagnostically, but no visible outcome consumer.

These are preserved 7 September controlled original-source/DOM results. Lifecycle callees were stubbed in the save witness; no native blocked-storage session or real-user reset was exercised. The result establishes missing caller feedback, not the prevalence of storage denial.

The invariant is: **a save failure preserves the usable in-memory choice and tells the user it is session-only; reset success is reported only if removing the saved configuration succeeded.** A success-shaped diagnostic or a future successful provider request cannot substitute for the storage result.

## Bind the repair and keep the existing storage contract

Before authorized work, record root, remote, HEAD and dirty paths:

~~~sh
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git remote get-url origin
git rev-parse HEAD
git status --short
git diff fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624 -- index.html config.js README.md tests/smoke.html
~~~

Expect theislampill/salah_widget. Stop on incompatible settings/applyConfig drift. [config.js saveLocal/clearLocal](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/config.js#L153) already catch storage errors and return {ok,error}; successful save additionally returns savedAt. Keep these shapes and the v1 key salah_widget:config:v1. No new storage library or version is required.

The writes are [applyConfig](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L2166), [_setStatus and form population](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L2283), [_commitSettings/_resetLocal/open/close](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L2399), narrowly associated settings feedback markup, and [README persistence wording](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/README.md#L126). [Candidate applyConfig](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/index.html#L2252) remains comparison evidence.

## Concrete state and staged implementation

The storage operation is synchronous even though applyConfig later awaits prayer loading. Publish its outcome **before the first await**; do not wait for network success to tell the user whether saving worked.

1. Retain a small transient latest persistence outcome at the settings owner: operation save/reset, status saved/session-only/cleared/reset-failed, and error name where present. This is proposed in-memory UI state, not a persisted schema. Reuse _storageErr for its existing diagnostic meaning and derive visible state from the same result. Let a successful later save/removal clear its earlier failure; a routine search hint or opening settings must not clear it.
2. In applyConfig's existing opts.save branch, consume the actual saveLocal return. On failure, publish "Changes apply for this session only. Could not save settings (SecurityError)." using safe textContent with a bounded known error label. On success, retain current origin/source/savedAt behavior and publish "Settings saved in this browser." Continue bindConfig, weather/prayer recovery and rendering on either outcome. Preserve session updates if storage is unavailable.
3. In _resetLocal, invalidate old lookup intent with the current form owner, then call clearLocal once and inspect its return. If removal fails, publish "Could not clear saved settings (SecurityError). Your saved settings remain." and stop this reset attempt before coarse detection or configuration replacement. The failure should not silently turn a saved London profile into a detected session profile. If removal succeeds, publish "Saved settings cleared. Detecting your area…" and run the existing detect path with save:false. A successful detection means "Saved settings cleared — using estimated area: …"; failed detection means "Saved settings cleared — enter your location." These states separately expose storage completion and detection completion.
4. Keep the existing settings close operation synchronous in its visible effect: commit the valid current form, close, restore the opener. Do not await prayer fetch or keep the modal trapped open because storage failed. _populateSettingsForm should show the retained persistence warning together with its ordinary search hint, instead of replacing the warning. A narrow status-composition helper can store the ordinary lookup message separately from the persistence outcome and write the existing #set-status; every existing _setStatus caller must still reach that renderer.
5. Supply a closed-panel indication without moving the card stack. Reuse the existing settings opener's generated .gear element as a warning marker "!" while session-only/reset-failed is current; restore the gear on success. Give the opener a state-bearing accessible name, for example "Widget settings — changes not saved; session only", and a matching title. Preserve the normal "Widget settings" name when no warning exists. Because #set-status is inside the hidden dialog after close, add one visually hidden polite live-status node outside that dialog, updated from the same outcome at the time of save/reset. The marker is a discoverable warning, and reopening shows the complete readable explanation. No toast framework, new modal or card-size change is warranted.

The live-status node and status compositor are justified only by real consumers: failure on close and subsequent reopen. Verify their reachability through _commitSettings and _resetLocal. A hidden node alone does not satisfy visible feedback; a punctuation marker alone does not explain the failure; both the named opener and full reopened status are required.

The alternative of throwing on save failure breaks session-only operation. Keeping settings open changes the documented autosave/close flow and can strand users behind a storage condition they cannot remedy. A status text assignment immediately followed by _populateSettingsForm still loses the message. Treating reset as a purge of all localStorage would exceed the configured-key contract and could destroy unrelated application data. Replacing localStorage or introducing migrations is unrelated to this caller bug.

## Public RED and deterministic matrix

Use original config.js with a Map-backed storage double in an isolated fixture; never alter the owner's actual origin. Load the real settings handlers and applyConfig; stub only provider/renderer lifecycle work where a pure fixture cannot run it. Mark that distinction in results. The decisive storage stimulus is:

~~~js
const bytes = new Map();
const storage = {
  getItem:k => bytes.has(k) ? bytes.get(k) : null,
  setItem:(k,v) => bytes.set(k,String(v)),
  removeItem:k => bytes.delete(k)
};
// Bind this object as the fixture window.localStorage before loading config.js.
// Seed through the production saveLocal before inducing the error:
SalahConfig.saveLocal({lat:51.5,lon:-0.12,label:"London",method:"3",units:"f"});
const oldBytes = bytes.get(SalahConfig.KEY);
// Reset RED:
storage.removeItem = () => { throw new DOMException("blocked","SecurityError"); };
// Click the actual Reset control; inspect status immediately and after any queued work.
// Required: no "cleared" success, oldBytes unchanged, zero new coarse-detect calls.
~~~

For save RED, use a fresh realm; seed first, make setItem throw the same exception, change set-units to c, dispatch input/change and close via the actual close path. Required live CONFIG.units is "c"; saved bytes retain the previous units; _storageErr is SecurityError; session-only feedback is observable without waiting for loadPrayerData.

| Case | Required storage, runtime and UI outcome |
|---|---|
| setItem SecurityError, valid current form | Session update succeeds; old saved bytes stay; warning marker/accessibility text and next-open full warning identify session-only. |
| removeItem SecurityError, saved London | No false cleared/reset message; saved bytes and live configuration remain; no new detection from this failed reset. |
| Successful save after a previous failure | New exact normalized settings are readable through loadLocal, source/origin provenance remains correct; warning clears. |
| Successful removal, detection pending | Config key is absent; cleared-plus-detecting message remains truthful. |
| Successful removal, detection fails | Key remains absent, manual setup is usable, no fabricated estimated area. |
| Successful removal, detection succeeds | applyConfig uses save:false; no accidental resaving of the reset default. |
| Blocked reads, malformed JSON or v2 record | Existing loadLocal null fallback remains; no uncaught error or destructive migration. |
| Unrelated prayer/weather/test key seeded | Save/reset leave those bytes unchanged. Reset is not a claim to erase location caches or provider records. |
| Current form supersedes pending reset/search | [R000F](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/15) rejects stale completion; no old callback clears or overwrites current feedback. |

Positive controls retain all 21 historical pure config assertions as supplementary checks; they already passed before this bug was repaired. Mutation controls remove result checking at save or reset, or restore _populateSettingsForm's unconditional hint: each corresponding UI-through-handler test must fail.
