Promotion and late reclassification from [R0005](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/5) may satisfy current data or make the next day eligible; they do not reset unrelated active operations. Existing rollover cooldown follows the same ownership/real-elapsed rules where shared hunks need integration.

Observable operation states are `eligible → attempt 1 → backoff → attempt 2 → backoff → attempt 3 → failed/cooldown → eligible`, with success or supersession terminal exits from any active attempt. UI state is distinct: a failed refresh may retain valid cache, while a failed cold load remains unavailable. Slot state is also distinct: a stale result can settle its own promise without being allowed to adopt or release a newer slot.

A bare `AbortController` does not bound a stalled body or ensure settlement. A deadline around headers alone leaves `r.json()` hanging. Starting a new outer operation on every frame defeats the three-attempt bound. A permanent failure bit solves the storm by recreating the cold-load dead end. A new global scheduler, automatic page reload, manual-refresh feature or complete offline app is unnecessary for these witnesses.

## Exact future verification matrix

All new results below must be produced on the final integrated tree; historical results above were controlled source execution, not browser PASS. Use actual source callers, virtual timeout/backoff scheduling, in-memory cache and deferred headers/body promises. Never change the host clock or the owner's storage.

| Input schedule | Expected repaired events and control |
|---|---|
| Headers never settle | Attempt 1 expires at nominal 10000 ms; attempts 2/3 follow after 900/1800 ms; no more than 3 attempts before operation settles nominally by 32700 ms. Owning busy state releases, timer registry has no live attempt timers, boot becomes able to start loop/error state. |
| Headers resolve immediately; body never settles | Same bound and release behavior. A headers-only timeout mutation must fail this row. |
| Body succeeds after its deadline; or old timeout fires after B starts | Late A cannot mutate current data, cache, error or B busy state. Current B success control still commits. |
| Two prompt failures, third valid record | Three calls; requested backoffs exactly 900/1800 ms; valid record commits once; no fourth retry. |
| No cache, all initial attempts fail; restore network before elapsed 60000 ms on same day | No per-frame calls during cooldown; first eligible visible opportunity at/after 60000 starts one operation and its healthy first response loads without reload or midnight. Capture request 4 and rendered recovery. |
| Same test with cache present and healthy | Cache paints through allowed admission; failed refresh does not blank it. No false “network current” claim. |
| Immediate failures with true virtual timer advancement and 66 opportunities t=0…65000 ms | Start operations only at 0 and 60000 ms if both are eligible and no data succeeds; at most 6 low-level calls. Record starts/attempts/waits separately. Compare the original source's saved 65 versus 6 witness using equivalent actual backoff accounting. |
| After successful tomorrow load, continue opportunities | Zero redundant tomorrow requests while the matching day record is usable. After promotion, the new nextDay becomes eligible once. |
| New generation/day while old operation is pending; wall +/−1 hour; frozen/accelerated simulation | New identity cannot inherit the old failure lock or be cleared by old finally. Eligibility follows real elapsed duration, not simulated minutes or wall correction, on a host with performance.now. |
| Hidden during cooldown, then resume late | No new background loop; one eligible operation on resume, no catch-up storm. |

Preserve original RED by temporarily removing deadline coverage, the cold-data scheduling branch, and the outer cooldown in separate authorized isolated mutations. Each must fail its corresponding row. Do not use a fixture that mocks `fetchTimings` to resolve immediately for the body-deadline assertion; that bypasses the failure. Do not collapse high-level operations and low-level requests into one count.

## Dependencies, public effect and closure

The accepted interface predecessor is [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3) for operation/attempt ownership. Coordinate prayer fetch/cache with [R0002](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/2), boot with [R0004](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/4) and [R0010](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/16), prefetch/adoption/render invalidation with [R0005](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/5), and clock/loop integration with [R0020](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/32). No new graph edge is required merely to share a fixture. One integrator owns shared production hunks.

Only transport lifecycle, existing scheduling opportunities and invoked tests should change. README should describe finite attempts, bounded same-day recovery, valid-cache behavior and visibility limits accurately; “offline-friendly” does not promise an offline application. No installer, preset, config schema, provider or dependency changes are justified. Preserve the existing single rAF loop, offscreen pause, reduced-motion override, readable 325×530 card and opaque moon. Final browser acceptance needs an unavailable→recovered crop and evidence that the default live scene still moves where conditions permit; a cloud hash is not motion evidence.

Rollback the coordinated deadline/cleanup/scheduler changes if healthy loads, ordinary retries or visibility behavior regress; keep explicit unavailable state and saved failure fixtures. A throttle-only patch, a deadline-only patch, or an automatic-retry patch with unbounded attempts is partial and cannot close #6. Closure needs final-tree traces for all three subcases, independent exact-tree review of ownership/cleanup, browser recovery readback and an evidence comment, with non-closing `Implements #6`. Public claims also require served-source/readback. Supplementary companion SHA256: `37d9e43da6e09af927fc51f3d8c227842e9039ba720db17aa947b6996425c40f`.

Identity provenance: first repository-local allocation batch; existing GitHub object order was used to assign distinct monotonic hex-4 IDs. Closed/held IDs are not reused. Issue number is not implementation priority.

title: R0005: Route prefetched and late prayer responses correctly across civil midnight
body:
<!-- salah-widget-audit-20260907:SW-005 -->
# R0005: Route prefetched and late prayer responses correctly across civil midnight

**Repository-local identity:** `R0005` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#5](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/5). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Campaign draft alias: SW-005. Existing corrective owner: GitHub #5. Proposed priority P1; product-or-skill defect. This work order specifies day adoption and its consumer invalidation; it does not authorize implementation or publish a repair.

## Three connected transitions, one owner

On main `fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624`, tomorrow's already-completed data is discarded when the loop notices midnight. In the recorded UTC September 7→8 fixture, the widget had today=September 7/Hijri 19 and tomorrow=September 8/Hijri 20. After Maghrib it displayed Hijri 20; offline midnight discarded tomorrow and retained September 7, so the display went backward to stale Hijri 19. Candidate `9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb` checks the prefetched Gregorian date, promotes September 8 and retains Hijri 20. That completed-promotion patch is a useful control.

A different scheduling witness fails on **both** trees. At September 7 23:59:59, dispatch tomorrow=September 8 and hold its promise. Cross midnight and let a rollover request load September 8. Release the older prefetch. Both end with `today.date=tomorrow.date="08-09-2026"`, never request September 9, and fail the next Maghrib advance; the candidate nevertheless reports `maghribRollApplied=true`. The callback assigns according to its original name “tomorrow,” even though its payload has become today. Promoting only records already completed at midnight does not repair that callback.

HA-N002 records the final transition: successful asynchronous new-day adoption can update data without causing a render. With a frozen simulation second, the displayed old date/stale flag remained through 20 callbacks. With ordinary advancing seconds, the next second repairs the sampled discrepancy. Therefore the supported claim is an adoption→consumer invalidation failure, not a guaranteed visible flash in every normal load.

These are retained exact-source controlled fixtures, not new browser runs or a claim about all Islamic calendar conventions. DATE-002, DATE-004 and HA-N002 are owned together because an admitted day must be placed in the right slot and become visible. Hijri date-selection/hold policy remains [R0009](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/9).

## Re-anchor and causal owner

Record actual checkout, HEAD and dirty state using `git -C C:\workspace\ai\salah_widget rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `rev-parse HEAD`, `status --short`, and `diff -- index.html tests/smoke.html` with that same prefix. Stop for relevant incompatible drift. Inspect [main prefetch callback](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L1986-L1990), [main midnight/adoption/render gate](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L2232-L2262), and [candidate completed promotion](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/index.html#L2321-L2353).

The existing `tomorrowStr()` increments a UTC-constructed civil date. Saved month/year/leap/DST controls passed on both trees. Its replacement with epoch+86400000 would introduce a separate bug. Preserve the actual calendar operation and define today/tomorrow by local civil identity at **adoption**, not 24-hour elapsed duration.

## Adoption contract and precise state table

The immutable context from [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3) establishes which configuration and operation still own the completion. Admission from [R0002](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/2) establishes that payload Gregorian identity equals its requested date. Only then classify it against `nowParts()` in the resolved location zone. Proposed design pseudocode below names decisions, not a new externally exposed schema:

```text
currentDay = location civil day at adoption
nextDay    = civil successor of currentDay
payloadDay = admitted response Gregorian day
obsolete generation/slot -> no adoption; settle only its own operation
payloadDay == currentDay -> eligible for today
payloadDay == nextDay    -> eligible for tomorrow
otherwise               -> no current/tomorrow adoption
```

| Before/completion | Required transition |
|---|---|
| Completed prefetched record now matches currentDay | Promote it to today **before** clearing tomorrow; persist under its actual date, clear stale, invalidate consumers. |
| In-flight prefetch becomes currentDay, today is absent/stale | Adopt as today; clear only matching old tomorrow state; release its own prefetch slot; allow nextDay acquisition. |
| Late prefetch becomes currentDay, a newer valid current record is already installed | Treat it as a duplicate no-op for today; do not overwrite the newer record or populate tomorrow with currentDay. Settle its own slot. |
| Prefetch still equals nextDay | Install as tomorrow if its context/operation remains eligible; current today stays intact; invalidate Hijri/Fajr consumers. |
| Completion arrives after an additional day of sleep or a backward date correction | If neither currentDay nor nextDay, discard from live slots. If it matches one, use that classification; an old dispatch label is not authority. |
| No matching cache/prefetch at a day transition | Retain old today only with stale state; leave current day unaccepted and recovery eligible under the bounded retry owner. |

1. Consolidate the repeated assignment bundle at the existing loader/prefetch/rollover boundaries: accepted payload and actual day, cache key from context, `lastDate`, stale flag, matching tomorrow clear/promotion, moon/star date invalidation and render-dirty signal. A narrow adoption function is justified only if those real callers use it. Do not move acquisition, provider validation, Hijri policy and all rendering into a generic state framework.
2. At midnight, test the completed prefetched record's admitted day and generation before consulting the current-day cache. Adopt the matching record before assigning `tomorrow=null`. Preserve valid cache fallback and the existing bounded offline retry opportunity. Never advance the accepted-day marker merely because the wall clock crossed; it advances only when current data was accepted. Any separate loop “observed day” marker must not suppress retries after a failed adoption.
3. Replace the unconditional prefetch `.then(d=>{tomorrow=d;...})` with the state table. Do the current-day/current-generation check after the promise settles. A current valid `today` obtained from a later rollover operation wins over a now-duplicate late prefetch; this avoids unnecessary stale-over-fresh replacement without inventing provider timestamps. Clear/release only the old operation's slot. A prior operation may not clear a newer prefetch busy state, per the ownership contract.
4. Reset prefetch eligibility by configuration and requested civil day through [R0006](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/6)'s scheduler state. Do not reset the cooldown every render or block September 9 because a non-null tomorrow happens to contain September 8. A valid nextDay record suppresses redundant requests; an invalid/wrong-day tomorrow slot does not. Successful promotion must leave the system capable of fetching the new nextDay.
5. Use a single coalesced render-dirty flag at accepted asynchronous state changes. The existing visible rAF loop renders when its simulated second changes **or** state is dirty, then consumes that dirty flag. A completion while hidden marks dirty; the first visible callback paints it without creating a second rAF loop. Keep existing explicit initial loader render where needed before loop startup. Do not call `render()` recursively from `model()` or every promise callback. Mark only after eligible adoption, not after rejected/obsolete results.
6. Preserve candidate moon/star invalidation details where the accepted day changes: `_starsProjected=false`, appropriate moon re-render/stamp invalidation and `lastMoonMin` reset. Those are consumers of an adopted day; arbitrary new celestial animation is out of scope. Preserve opaque calendar moon and the existing visible-motion/reduced-motion contract.

Rejected alternatives matter here. Unconditionally clearing tomorrow cures neither late callbacks nor offline loss. Rejecting all responses dispatched before midnight throws away useful current-day data. A global “date never decreases” rule would hide backward device corrections and provider anomalies; it cannot establish current Gregorian identity. Rendering from every callback creates repeated work and can recurse into another prefetch; one invalidation consumed by the existing loop is sufficient.

## Deterministic RED, GREEN and mutation controls

Build a disposable controlled-clock fixture using actual prefetch callback and `startRenderLoop`, with in-memory fetch/cache and paint capture. Synthetic record `P(day,hijriDay)` has matching Gregorian fields, UTC metadata, six usable clocks Fajr 05:00, Sunrise 06:00, Dhuhr 12:00, Asr 15:30, Maghrib/Sunset 18:00, Isha 19:30, and Hijri year 1448/month 2 with the supplied day. These dates/times are fixture inputs, not a provider calendar claim.

| Recipe | Required observable final result |
|---|---|
| Start `2026-09-07T23:59:59Z`, today=P(7,19), completed tomorrow=P(8,20), network offline; advance 2 seconds | today/lastDate September 8, stale false, persisted September 8, current Hijri selection 20 under existing Maghrib policy. Historical main produced stale September 7/Hijri 19; candidate promotion is the useful positive branch. |
| Same start, hold first request for September 8; cross midnight, release rollover September 8, then release old prefetch September 8 | today September 8; tomorrow is absent or September 9, never September 8; old response does not replace newer accepted data; September 9 becomes requestable. Advance through next Maghrib and observe its correct next-day consumer. |
| Release prefetch September 8 after midnight while rollover fails | Late response may repair current today, clear stale, and persist its actual day. Blanket rejection of pre-midnight requests fails this control. |
| Release normally before midnight | Store September 8 only in tomorrow, keep September 7 today, preserve pre-Maghrib preview and later Maghrib selection. |
| Switch configuration before old completion; or release September 8 after current day September 9 | No old-generation mutation; no stale September 8 installed as current/tomorrow on September 9; owning current operation remains busy until its own completion. |
| Frozen `simTime`, stale old record, release a valid current-day response after the last paint | The **first next visible frame** consumes dirty state and paints adopted day/stale=false without changing simulated seconds; 20 further callbacks cannot retain old output or produce redundant per-frame fetches. Hide before release and verify the first resumed frame. |
| Year/month/leap controls | Keep Dec 31→Jan 1, Feb 28 2024→Feb 29→Mar 1 and New York DST civil-next-day results. No arithmetic replacement by fixed elapsed 24h. |

Capture request dates, operation IDs, loaded/next-day slots, accepted date, stale flag, selected/displayed date and cache writes at every release point. A final screenshot alone can miss a poisoned tomorrow slot; a final state number alone can miss a frozen consumer. Browser date/status crops must supplement source witnesses. Temporarily disable promotion, restore unconditional tomorrow assignment, and disable render-dirty consumption separately in an authorized isolated fixture: each matching test must fail. Restore final source before qualifying it.

## Integration and closeable boundary

Accepted interface predecessors are [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3) for requesting-context ownership and [R0004](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/4) for location-day boot; [R0002](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/2) supplies final valid-day qualification. This owner supplies current/promotion state to [R0009](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/9). Shared production hunks with [R0006](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/6) (eligibility/retry) and [R0020](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/32) (forward/backward current instant) require one integrator, not competing edits to the loop. Preserve the existing relationship graph; a common `index.html` does not make every other issue a predecessor.

Change the adoption/callback/render-invalidation paths and their invoked fixtures. Update DESIGN/HANDOFF or README where they explain midnight, retained stale data or frozen-scene refresh; do not claim a new prayer calculation or Hijri authority. Main cache identity, builder/config output, install scripts and presets remain compatible. The public surface is a correct current day and responsive date consumer within the existing readable 325×530 card.

If candidate promotion is integrated but late prefetch or frozen repaint still fails, record that partial state and keep #5 open. Revert the coordinated day assignments/invalidation changes if valid cache, ordinary prefetch or rendering regresses; preserve old cache bytes and failure evidence. Acceptance requires final-tree transition/control results, independent review of caller reachability, and actual rendered readback before an evidence comment and manual closure. Use non-closing `Implements #5`; served-source/readback is additionally required for deployment claims. Supplementary historical companion SHA256: `2c7bf3fff141c5d1d9fd5f7b4ad3a6aaa4ee1d7159bfb075eae54b30f0da42ec`. The decisive public inputs above do not require the private companion.

Identity provenance: first repository-local allocation batch; existing GitHub object order was used to assign distinct monotonic hex-4 IDs. Closed/held IDs are not reused. Issue number is not implementation priority.

title: R0004: Choose the initial prayer day in the resolved location timezone without losing legacy cache
body:
<!-- salah-widget-audit-20260907:SW-004 -->
# R0004: Choose the initial prayer day in the resolved location timezone without losing legacy cache

**Repository-local identity:** `R0004` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#4](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/4). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Campaign draft alias: SW-004. Existing corrective owner: GitHub #4. Proposed priority P1; product-or-skill defect, including its discriminating boot fixture. This plan grants no implementation or publication authority.

## Incident, useful candidate work and rejected premise

At controlled instant `2026-09-07T22:00:00Z`, New York is still September 7 while Tokyo is September 8. An embed selecting Tokyo coordinates without a `tz` hint starts with the default `America/New_York` hint. Main `fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624` requests `07-09-2026`, adopts the returned `Asia/Tokyo` zone, and paints September 7 as current while `nowParts()` says September 8. Its recorded request sequence was September 7 then September 9 prefetch. Candidate `9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb` rederives the live day and requests September 7, September 8, then September 9; its first accepted live paint is September 8. That live correction is useful, but it is not a complete loader repair.

Both versions filter cache by the hint's September 7 **before** reading the cached location zone. A valid September 8 Tokyo record therefore cannot boot offline. Conversely, a September 7 record passes that early filter, then sets Tokyo and paints as current although the local day is September 8. The candidate's date-truth readout records the mismatch while still calling it current. Diagnostic visibility does not enforce the invariant.

The candidate also removes `_cacheTz` from the persistent key. Historical DATE-014 copied a valid current-day main cache into identical offline storage: main loaded; candidate reported `Could not load prayer times`. The stated motivation that provider-zone adoption orphans main's key was contradicted by execution: main's key stayed `salah:35.68|139.69|America/New_York|2|0` before and after `tz` became Tokyo. `_cacheTz` was captured from configuration. Candidate's stable key was `salah:35.68|139.69|2|0`. Do not turn a false key-instability premise into an unnecessary destructive migration.

These DATE-001/003/012/014 results are saved exact-source Node VM observations with controlled clock, network, storage and paint records, not screenshots or proof of a live service incident. The explicit-zone control passes on both trees; therefore a smoke that supplies the correct zone cannot detect the omitted-zone defect. Provider-zone resolution itself is intentional: `tz` is a first-paint hint, not a force-the-provider override.

## Re-anchor and owned files

Record the future execution checkout, HEAD and dirty state using `git -C C:\workspace\ai\salah_widget rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `rev-parse HEAD`, `status --short`, and `diff -- index.html tests/smoke.html README.md ARCHITECTURE.md` with the same prefix. Stop on incompatible cache/adoption drift; retain unrelated work and old cache bytes. The source references are [main key and cache helpers](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L735-L757), [main loader](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L2143-L2154), [candidate live correction](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/index.html#L2218-L2238), [candidate cache identity](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/index.html#L745-L755), and [candidate date smoke](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/tests/smoke.html#L201-L229).

The invariant is about the **first accepted current paint**, including a cached paint: its admitted Gregorian day must equal the selected location's civil day at adoption. Valid offline data must survive upgrade. It does not promise a cached tomorrow across every reload, a new multi-day cache, a user-selected calendar ruling, or a forced timezone override.

## Ordered loader design and observable states

Use the context supplied by [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3) and admission supplied by [R0002](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/2). The states below can remain local variables and existing UI state; no persisted state machine is required.

| Stage | May be known | Permitted effect |
|---|---|---|
| `hint-only` | Selected coordinates/method/school; first-paint zone hint; request generation | Show loading/unavailable; no unverified record painted current. |
| `zone-known` | Admitted cached/provider timezone and valid request/body date agreement | Derive civil day at the current instant in that zone. Metadata adoption is generation-guarded. |
| `current-record` | Payload day equals the just-derived location day | Commit today, accepted date, cache and current status, then render. |
| `needs-corrected-day` | Zone valid, available payload belongs to another day | Keep unavailable or explicitly stale retained data; dispatch at most one corrected-day request in this load operation. |
| `unavailable/retry-eligible` | Correct-day transport failed or civil day moved again | Settle this load; leave bounded recovery to the existing liveness owner. Do not recurse indefinitely during accelerated simulation. |

1. Split reading the selected cache envelope from its day filter. Read only deterministic keys for the selected configuration, in a try/catch; never scan all localStorage. Validate envelope/data identity first. An admitted envelope supplies its own stored day for request/body comparison and a usable location zone even if its day will not qualify as today. This permits discovery of Tokyo from a September 8 record that the old hint would have hidden. Invalid cache is a miss, not authority for timezone mutation.
2. The selected repair target is main `fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624`. Retain its exact timezone-bearing `salah:[lat]|[lon]|[_cacheTz]|[method]|[school]` namespace for both reads and writes. Read only the captured key for the selected configuration; provider-zone adoption changes `tz`, never `_cacheTz` or the captured key. Do not add the audit candidate's zone-free fallback adapter, scan another namespace, migrate entries, or delete its bytes. Candidate `9d9c` is comparison evidence, not an assumed installed cohort or future target. A zone-free-only entry is a miss on this main-based repair; the normal bounded network/error path follows, just as the namespace contract requires. If a later authorized target actually includes a shipped alternate schema, stop at that incompatible drift and reconcile its upgrade requirement separately before changing this decision. The known upgrade control here is existing main-format cache remaining readable after this main-based repair.
3. Once an eligible cached record supplies a valid zone, derive the selected civil day **then** compare its payload day. If matching, assign current state and render; continue the existing live refresh without blanking valid cache on failure. If not matching, keep no current paint. An intentionally retained old record must be marked stale before rendering, with its actual day intact; whether stale details are displayed is consumed by [R0009](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/9), not solved by relabeling the record here.
4. With no usable cached zone, request the hint-derived day as the bootstrap request. Its response must pass request/body admission. Capture its returned zone locally, check current request ownership, then resolve the location day using that zone and the current instant. A valid but wrong-for-now response can establish the zone without becoming today. If the location day differs, request that corrected date once, still within the captured generation. Avoid saving the bootstrap record as current under a corrected date.
5. At the corrected response, recheck ownership and civil day again. A response for the originally corrected date is not necessarily current after midnight or a clock step. Return it to the day-classification contract of [R0005](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/5); if no record qualifies, settle and schedule bounded recovery via [R0006](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/6). A busy flag cannot remain held while waiting for an impossible date match. The useful candidate second fetch is retained with this final check; no unlimited fetch-until-day-stops-changing loop is introduced.
6. Commit zone/current data/accepted date/stale flag/cache as one synchronous eligible adoption, then notify the existing render path. Do not let a cached render run between `today=cached` and day validation. Bootstrap metadata from obsolete A must not alter B. Preserve intentional simulation reanchoring on settled timezone through the clock owners; do not “fix” the boot case by setting the machine clock or forcing every embed to include `tz`.

Keeping the existing key is smaller than migration and preserves known offline consumers. Forcing the correct zone in builder output would conceal the loader defect and make existing embeds remain wrong. Suppressing all cache use would avoid the bad paint but deliberately break offline behavior. Adopting the whole candidate supplies a useful live patch while importing an observed cache regression. All three are rejected alternatives.

## Deterministic fixtures and expected transitions

Use an isolated storage origin. Set the fixture clock to `2026-09-07T22:00:00Z`, device/hint zone New York, selected coordinates `35.68,139.69`, method `2`, school `0`, and **omit the URL/config timezone hint** for the negative stimulus. Return successful synthetic prayer records for the day requested in `/v1/timings/DD-MM-YYYY`, with `meta.timezone:"Asia/Tokyo"`, matching Gregorian fields and usable fixed timings (Fajr 05:00, Sunrise 06:00, Dhuhr 12:00, Asr 15:30, Maghrib/Sunset 18:00, Isha 19:30). The particular times are fixture values, not Tokyo prayer predictions. Record every request and every paint's loaded day, effective zone, current location day and stale/unavailable state.

| Fixture | RED preserved / final expected result |
|---|---|
| Empty storage, no hint, live success | Main historically painted September 7 current. Final bootstrap request September 7 may occur, but only September 8 can first paint current; corrected request is September 8. Subsequent next-day prefetch may be September 9. |
| Exact same setup with explicit `tz=Asia/Tokyo` | Positive control: first current request/paint September 8; no needless September 7 correction. This control alone cannot pass the issue. |
| Same-day-in-both-zones instant, e.g. `2026-09-07T12:00:00Z` | Correct September 7 load; no extra corrected-day fetch merely because zone names differ. |
| Main-format key holds `{date:"08-09-2026",data:<valid Tokyo September 8 record>}`, network offline | Read metadata before day filtering, adopt Tokyo, paint September 8 current from cache. Leave bytes/key available for rollback. |
| Same key holds valid Tokyo September 7, network offline | No paint calling September 7 current after Tokyo day September 8 is known. Retained old display, if any, is explicitly stale and keeps September 7. |
| Valid old main cache copied unchanged into repaired isolated storage | Offline current-day function preserved. Compare key strings/bytes and resulting data, not only cache-reader return. An exact zone-free-only candidate key is a negative namespace control: it is not adopted or deleted. With both keys present, use only the valid main-format selected key. |
| Corrupt JSON, timings null, invalid zone, or envelope/payload date mismatch | No trusted zone/data adoption from the record; healthy network fallback remains reachable. Optional absent Hijri is distinct from required invalid Gregorian identity. |
| Corrected request held across midnight or a config switch | Re-evaluate day and generation before adoption. Old generation cannot mutate zone/cache/current state; same-generation day change is reclassified rather than mislabeled. |

A browser test must observe the first qualified paint, not merely wait for a final “eventually correct” state. Record loading→zone discovery→first current frame on the disposable origin, with a crop of the date/status row. Do not call a live-network timeout PASS or SKIP the deterministic negative because the service is down. Temporarily restoring the early day filter or removing the post-response day check in an isolated fixture must fail the matching row; explicit-zone control remains green. Retain month/year/leap/DST civil-tomorrow controls unchanged because this issue does not replace calendar arithmetic.

## Interfaces, public surfaces and done

Accepted dependencies stay [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3) → this owner for request-context interface and [R0002](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/2) → this owner for final admission qualification. This owner supplies initial location-day behavior to [R0005](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/5). Coordinate prayer-cache/boot/adoption hunks with those owners and [R0006](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/6), [R0010](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/16); one integrator handles shared tests/docs insertions. No whole-issue serialization is implied.

Update only loader/cache behavior and its actual invoked fixtures. README/ARCHITECTURE should explain location timezone resolution, current-day acceptance and retained offline compatibility. Builder may continue intentionally omitting `tz`; no new setting, installer, preset, API provider or calendar library is needed. Retain the 325×530 frame and readable loading/date states without changing the sky renderer.

Revert the narrow loader changes if valid main-format cache or normal online boot regresses; keep original cache bytes, never purge them. A live-only corrected-day pass leaves this issue partial until wrong/current cache, upgrade and first-paint controls pass. Close #4 only after final-tree results, independent source/caller review and browser first-paint evidence are recorded in an evidence comment, using non-closing `Implements #4`. Public claims additionally require matching served source/readback. Supplementary historical companion SHA256: `b34a311eb148cdc8a6d96c7068894bd0587c26b50175720701c3e65ab4ad705e`.

Identity provenance: first repository-local allocation batch; existing GitHub object order was used to assign distinct monotonic hex-4 IDs. Closed/held IDs are not reused. Issue number is not implementation priority.

title: R0003: Bind asynchronous prayer, weather and radar commits to their requesting configuration
body:
<!-- salah-widget-audit-20260907:SW-003 -->
# R0003: Bind asynchronous prayer, weather and radar commits to their requesting configuration

**Repository-local identity:** `R0003` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#3](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Campaign draft alias: SW-003. Existing corrective owner: GitHub #3. Proposed priority P1; product-or-skill defect. Filing this plan neither implements it nor authorizes a merge or deployment.

## The missing ownership contract

A result must belong to the selection that dispatched it, and a completion must release only the operation/attempt that owns its slot. Resetting globals when settings change does neither. On both main `fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624` and unmerged candidate `9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb`, the saved PROVIDER-01 fixture selected Madinah A, then New York B, completed B, and finally completed A. New York's label and coordinates survived, but A changed the global timezone to `Asia/Riyadh`, changed next Asr from `15:30` to `15:49`, and wrote A's data under B's cache key. A delayed tomorrow response likewise entered B's tomorrow slot.

W004 witnesses the same missing contract in another acquisition path. A Madinah Celsius request remained busy across selection of London `(51.48,-0.001)` in Fahrenheit, preventing the new request. Its eventual temperature `20` was installed and persisted under `salahwx:51.48|-0.001|f`. An old RainViewer tile completed after the switch and restored `precipMm:4.3` for the old location. An hourly New York record was converted using the new global Riyadh zone: expected epoch `1788814800000`, actual `1788789600000`, a −7-hour error. These are controlled exact-source scheduling results, not observations of those cities' weather or a live provider incident.

The causal sequence is dispatch from globals → asynchronous wait → completion reads different globals → mutation of shared state/persistence. Prayer transport mutates `tz` before the caller can reject the data; weather computes `wxKey()` at completion; radar computes coordinates after its manifest await and accepts a later image callback; unqualified `finally` clears global busy flags. An abort signal alone cannot establish correctness when an already-resolved body or image callback still runs.

## Re-anchor the exact owners

Before edits, record `git -C C:\workspace\ai\salah_widget rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `rev-parse HEAD`, `status --short`, and `diff -- index.html tests/smoke.html` with the same `git -C` prefix. Compare [prayer fetch/cache](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L735-L757), [weather dispatch and hourly completion](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L771-L801), [radar manifest/image completion](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L820-L840), [prefetch](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L1986-L1990), and [load/reset/apply](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L2143-L2179). Stop on incompatible relevant drift and obtain a revised integration boundary. The candidate has the same ownership defect; its unrelated changes are not authorized by this issue.

## Proposed in-memory interface and transitions

Agree this internal shape before shared edits. Names below are design pseudocode, not fields already present in a public API or a persisted schema:

```text
context = { generation, operationId, kind, requestedDay,
            lat, lon, method, school, units, requestZone, cacheKey }
attempt = { operationId, attemptId, controller }
eligible(context, slot) = context.generation == currentGeneration
                         and slot.operationId == context.operationId
```

Capture primitives before the first await. Prayer contexts include day/method/school and the exact main-format cache key; weather includes units and the timezone actually encoded in its URL; radar includes coordinates for manifest→tile→pixel work. `kind` identifies the dispatch slot, not a permanent promise that tomorrow data will remain tomorrow. Missing/unneeded fields need not be added to every record. Each retry gets its own attempt identity under one operation identity; the operation owns the busy slot across backoff. Distinguish a configuration generation from attempt identity: A→B→A requires three generations even if the third selection equals the first by value.

1. Increment the acquisition generation at the accepted configuration replacement boundary before clearing/loading state. Bind the new config, invalidate old operation eligibility, and then dispatch current work. Do not wait for old `finally` to make B eligible. Slot replacement is synchronous; optionally abort superseded transports after their identity has become ineligible. A pure label/date-format edit must not cause an uncontrolled parallel acquisition path; preserve the existing apply boundary unless an explicit optimization is separately justified.
2. Make `fetchTimings` return admitted payload data without mutating global timezone. Capture its URL inputs once. At loader, prefetch and rollover completions, first validate request/body agreement through [R0002](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/2), then check generation/slot ownership, then pass the payload and context into the day-classification path. Only the accepted adoption branch may change `tz`, today/tomorrow, dates, stale status, cache or render invalidation. The bootstrap timezone discovery owned by [R0004](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/4) is itself a guarded adoption of metadata; it is not an exception permitting old A to change B's zone.
3. In `fetchWeather`, parse/normalize into local candidate values, including elevation, current weather, source timestamps and track. An old completion changes none of `siteElev`, `weather`, `weatherTrack`, `lastWxAt` or storage. Compute the exact cache key from the captured context, never the current globals. Check ownership before persistence as well as before the visible assignment. Preserve weather validation/freshness decisions for their owners; being current-generation does not make an invalid or old observation fresh.
4. Consume [R0008](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/8)'s explicit-zone conversion interface at the **existing** hourly parser. Pass `context.requestZone` through the converter and its strict round-trip check; a wrapper that captures the zone but calls a helper which rereads global `tz` is still wrong. The request zone is the zone used to encode the response wall strings. If returned metadata contradicts it, fail that track closed or reconcile explicitly; do not reinterpret the same string using whichever zone is globally selected at completion. Invalid/unresolved gap or fold conversions cannot supply fresh-weather epochs to [R000B](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/11).
5. In `fetchRadar`, derive tile coordinates and sample pixel coordinates from captured lat/lon, even after the manifest await. Hold frame/source data locally across image loading. After load/error, gate the final `weatherRadar` assignment and operation cleanup. An old tile can settle its own promise but may not restore old precipitation, clear a replacement radar slot, or reset its retry deadline. Image deadline/handler cleanup is [R000D](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/13)'s interface consumer, not a second lifecycle implementation here.
6. In all success, catch and finally paths, release the slot only if its operation ID still matches; clear an attempt timer/controller only if its attempt ID matches. An old catch must not show a current error over B, and an old finally must not make B's busy state false. Current success and current failure must both eventually settle normally. Do not retain one global `wxBusy` lock across generations and call that stale protection.

This is a few contexts and existing slot guards, not a global scheduler, persisted request log, or freshness bit. A universal shared bit would let unrelated weather completion invalidate a prayer request. Comparing only coordinates misses units/method/school and A→B→A. Capturing only the cache key still permits cross-location state and timezone mutation. Serializing all requests behind A prevents B from loading when A hangs. Cancellation remains useful resource cleanup, with identity checks as the acceptance proof.

## Deterministic acceptance, with actual caller reachability

Create deferred fetch/body/image promises in an isolated fixture; execute actual `applyConfig`, fetch, adoption and render paths. Keep an in-memory storage write log. For the historical prayer recipe, hold `nowParts()` at September 7, 2026 noon to isolate ownership from date arithmetic. A is `(24.47,39.61,"Madinah",method 4,school 0,initial tz UTC)` and B is `(40.71,-74.01,"New York",method 2,school 0,initial tz UTC)`. Both responses are successful envelopes for `07-09-2026`, with Sunrise 06:00, Dhuhr 12:00, Sunset/Maghrib 18:00 and Isha 19:30. A has Fajr 04:46, Asr 15:49 and `meta.timezone:"Asia/Riyadh"`; B has Fajr 05:00, Asr 15:30 and `meta.timezone:"America/New_York"`. Supply valid Gregorian identity and optional date fixtures under the admission contract. Dispatch A, dispatch B, release B, snapshot, release A, snapshot again.

The repaired final snapshot must equal B's snapshot for coordinates, label, zone, schedule, tomorrow, stale status and cache bytes. Record B's captured cache key; after A releases there must be no write to B's key. A's late completion must also make no new stale-cache write after it is obsolete. Reverse completion order as a positive current-owner control; do not assert “nothing ever commits.”

| Interleaving/control | Specific required outcome |
|---|---|
| A→B, old success / rejection / finally after B | No B state, error, cache or busy-slot change from A. B's own completion still releases its slot. |
| A→B→A with first A released last | Only third-generation A may commit. Equality of coordinates does not resurrect first A. |
| Same coordinates, method-only or school-only change | Old schedule cannot overwrite the newly selected method/school; captured request URL and cache identity match the winner. |
| Madinah Celsius request → London Fahrenheit selection | Current London work can dispatch while old work settles; old `20` cannot enter London cache or live state. Healthy London response commits through the same path. |
| Old hourly `2026-03-08T03:30` from New York; global zone becomes Riyadh | Pure conversion with captured New York zone is `2026-03-08T07:30:00.000Z`, not `08:30Z` or a Riyadh-derived instant. Obsolete generation cannot commit it. Equivalent current-generation control may commit. This combined DST fixture is proposed acceptance, not a previously executed result. |
| Radar manifest released before switch, image released after switch; and manifest released after switch | Old tile/pixel sampling uses A coordinates, but no old rain evidence enters B; B's slot survives A cleanup. Current tile positive control retains existing precipitation gating. |
| Same-generation tomorrow crosses midnight | Context remains generation-valid; [R0005](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/5) classifies its actual date. Rejecting every late response is not an acceptable shortcut. |
| Healthy cache reload after winning response | Reload isolated storage and recover B, proving ownership reaches persistence rather than only UI assignment. |

Mutation controls remove a timezone commit guard, change a captured cache-key write back to `cacheKey()`/`wxKey()`, and make old `finally` unconditional, separately in an authorized disposable fixture. The corresponding row must fail each time. Removing only an abort signal should **not** defeat stale-result rejection. That control distinguishes ownership from transport luck.

## Integration, public effects and closure

The accepted directed interface is [R0008](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/8) → this owner: converter semantics there, captured request-zone/hourly caller here. This owner supplies request/attempt ownership to [R0004](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/4), [R0005](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/5), [R0006](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/6), and [R000D](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/13). Coordinate exact writes with prayer admission/cache, weather admission/age, radar truth, zero-coordinate and config-apply owners [R0002](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/2), [R000B](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/11), [R000C](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/12), [R000E](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/14), [R001E](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/30), [R0011](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/17). Agree interfaces before shared hunks; these are not whole-issue serialization dependencies. UI lookup intent remains [R000F](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/15).

Only acquisition/adoption code and discriminating tests should change. Preserve main legacy cache keys and valid old bytes, config serialization, builder, installers and presets. README needs an update only if stale/loading behavior visible to users changes. No new provider, dependency, schema migration or visual redesign is needed. Final browser evidence must show actual settings changes with controlled responses and readable 325×530 output; preserve opaque moon and scene motion rather than using races as a reason to freeze rendering.

Revert dispatch and all dependent completion guards together if current requests cease to settle; a half-installed context interface is unsafe. Stop on a missing consumer guard, ambiguous shared writer or contradictory cache result and retain an explicit partial state. Close #3 only after final-tree race/control results, independent exact-tree review of every mutation site, and an evidence comment; use `Implements #3` without auto-close. Public claims require matching served-source and consumer readback. Supplementary historical companion SHA256: `daf4ee3c022f3b5717ad67b03d78433451389c3639ff6ae5c43ab7384d8707b5`.

Identity provenance: first repository-local allocation batch; existing GitHub object order was used to assign distinct monotonic hex-4 IDs. Closed/held IDs are not reused. Issue number is not implementation priority.

title: R0002: Validate prayer records before network or cached data enters model state
body:
<!-- salah-widget-audit-20260907:SW-002 -->
# R0002: Validate prayer records before network or cached data enters model state

**Repository-local identity:** `R0002` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#2](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/2). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


Campaign draft alias: SW-002. Existing corrective owner: GitHub #2. Proposed priority P1; product-or-skill defect. This is a repair work order, not permission to implement or a claim that a repair has shipped.

## Failure being repaired and evidence boundary

The prayer boundary currently asks whether `data.timings` is truthy, then permits timezone mutation, model use and persistence. Truthiness does not establish a usable schedule. At main `fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624` and candidate `9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb`, historical controlled execution admitted an empty object, admitted a September 6 body for a September 7 request, and admitted a nonfinite Dhuhr value. Separately, a corrupt cache threw before live recovery was entered. These are one ingress/usable-record invariant with different reachable entrances.

The preserved PROVIDER-02/DATE-008 results establish these exact consequences: `{data:{timings:{}}}` was accepted after one request and produced `NaN:undefined`; `Dhuhr:"1e999:00"` parsed to `Infinity`, and execution of the actual `model()` exceeded the fixture's 1000 ms VM containment limit; `{date:"07-09-2026",data:{timings:null,meta:{timezone:"UTC"}}}` in the selected cache caused a throw with **zero** calls to a healthy network stub. A `06-09-2026` payload was painted under a `07-09-2026` request with `stale=false`. A conventional 400 envelope without truthy timings was already rejected after three attempts. Thus this is not evidence that all provider errors are accepted.

DATE-007 adds an independent consumer boundary: `fmtDate({})` returned `undefined-00-NaN` on main; candidate's presence guard handled that case but both returned `1448-00-NaN` for a nonnumeric day and empty month, returned `1448-99-99` for invalid ranges, and threw `mon.slice is not a function` for numeric `month.en`. SEC-010's initially weak nonfinite lead was corroborated by the provider reproducer. These were exact-source Node VM tests with controlled fetch/storage/clock and model/DOM substitutes, not a production provider incident, browser hang-duration measurement, or pixel verdict.

## Re-anchor and preserve the existing contracts

Before future edits, run `git -C C:\workspace\ai\salah_widget rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `git -C C:\workspace\ai\salah_widget rev-parse HEAD`, `git -C C:\workspace\ai\salah_widget status --short`, and `git -C C:\workspace\ai\salah_widget diff -- index.html config.js tests/smoke.html`. Record the actual base and relevant dirty hunks. Compare the functions below with the pinned source; stop for owner reconciliation if their admission or cache contracts have materially changed. Do not import the candidate branch wholesale or overwrite unrelated research files.

The production owners are [clock/date parsing and `fmtDate`](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L673-L692), [cache and `fetchTimings(dateStr)`](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L735-L757), [`model()` normalization](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L1201-L1224), and [`loadPrayerData()`](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L2143-L2154). The [candidate formatter](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/index.html#L696-L701) is a partial presence guard, not sufficient admission.

Preserve the six required model events `Fajr, Sunrise, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha`; `Sunset` is optional and the existing Maghrib fallback remains. Valid coincident polar values are permitted. The captured Tromso summer control has Fajr/Sunrise/Sunset/Maghrib/Isha all `00:46`; winter sunrise/sunset are `11:42`. Both trees produced finite model/arc results for those records. A rule requiring strict increasing order would introduce a regression.

## Smallest executable repair design

1. Put one small admission routine beside the current prayer fetch/cache helpers. Its proposed inputs are raw provider data plus the requested Gregorian date; its result is either a usable record or an explicit invalid result. This is a proposed internal interface, not an existing API. Keep provider field names and the persisted `{date,data}` envelope; normalize only fields consumed by the widget. Do not persist a second schema or invent missing calendar values.
2. At the network entrance require `Response.ok`, an object envelope, and no contradictory provider error code/status. Successful test doubles must model the chosen envelope rule; a stub omitting `ok` must not accidentally qualify an HTTP check. Validate before changing `tz`, returning accepted data, or writing cache. Required clocks accept the documented `HH:mm` form and optional parenthesized zone suffix, with hours 00–23 and minutes 00–59 after trimming. Reject exponents, missing components, nonfinite numbers, extra numeric components, and out-of-range values. The exact accepted grammar should be a narrow anchored expression; `clean()` followed by unrestricted `Number()` is not that grammar. Preserve the display string or a normalized equivalent that keeps existing 12/24-hour output.
3. Require a usable IANA timezone: construction/formatting by `Intl.DateTimeFormat` must succeed for the supplied zone. Do not use `partsInTz`'s browser-local fallback as proof that an invalid provider zone was valid. Gregorian identity must be a real calendar date and equal the requested `DD-MM-YYYY`: require month 1–12, a positive integer year, and a day that survives a strict Gregorian calendar round trip without Date.UTC normalizing it into another month; where `date`, day/month/year primitives coexist, they must agree. A September 6 body is invalid for a September 7 request even if its times look plausible. Midnight reclassification is downstream and does not relax this request/body agreement.
4. Cache reads parse the existing envelope in a guarded boundary, validate its `data` against the envelope date, and treat malformed contents as a miss. The caller can then resolve the selected location day under [R0004](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/4). An invalid cache may neither assign `today` nor throw past the live-fetch recovery path. Leave old bytes in place if storage is unavailable; a valid live record can replace the selected entry through the existing save path. A failed write must not invalidate valid in-memory data.
5. Keep optional display data optional. Missing Hijri data or a missing optional month name does not invalidate otherwise usable prayer times. `fmtDate` must validate finite integer year/month/day before constructing tokens; For optional Hijri primitives, accept month 1–12 and day 1–30 with a positive integer year; this structural bound does not calculate the true length of a particular Hijri month or fabricate a calendar conversion. Do not treat arbitrary year 1448 as Gregorian evidence. For malformed optional data return the existing empty/unavailable representation, allowing the date-output owner to disclose it. Require string names before `.slice`; for numeric-only token formats a missing name must not invent one. Preserve longest-token replacement and the valid output `1448 48 Safar Saf 02 2 19 19` for `YYYY YY MMMM MMM MM M DD D` with day 19, month 2/Safar, year 1448.
6. Add a finite-input guard at the model normalization boundary as defense against an accidental internal bypass. An invalid model input must produce an explicit unavailable/error path without entering either `while` loop. Do not silently coerce Infinity to zero or cap it at an arbitrary valid-looking prayer time. The ingress rejection is primary; this guard bounds the failure if a future caller violates it.
7. Repair the existing missing-config date-format fallback at [the `_P` lookup](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L616-L622) with an own-property alias check and a string fallback. HA-N001 reproduced `constructor` and `__proto__` becoming nonstrings when `config.js` was unavailable; `toString`, `valueOf`, and `hasOwnProperty` did **not** reproduce because lowercasing changed those keys. Normal config normalization masks this path. Keep unsupported literal strings literal; applying `String()` only at `.replace` would stringify an inherited function instead of preserving the requested literal. The normal [config alias/normalization path](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/config.js#L39-L81) is a compatibility control, not a mandate to expand this repair into config serialization.

Admission must return before any commit on rejection. Request ownership, timeout cleanup and day selection remain separate decisions. The integration order is admission return contract, network/cache callers, model/date defenses, then shared caller qualification. One integrator owns overlapping edits with [R0003](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/3), [R0004](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/4), and [R0006](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/6).

## Public deterministic RED → GREEN recipe

Use an isolated origin or a VM containing the actual source blocks/callers, with in-memory storage and a controlled September 7, 2026 noon clock. Copy this **synthetic test fixture**, not a purported live record; return it under `{code:200,data:record}` with `ok:true,status:200`:

```json
{"timings":{"Fajr":"05:00","Sunrise":"06:00","Dhuhr":"12:00","Asr":"15:30","Sunset":"18:00","Maghrib":"18:00","Isha":"19:30"},"date":{"gregorian":{"date":"07-09-2026","day":"07","month":{"number":9,"en":"September"},"year":"2026"},"hijri":{"date":"19-02-1448","day":"19","month":{"number":2,"en":"Safar"},"year":"1448"}},"meta":{"timezone":"UTC"}}
```

For each mutation below, drive `loadPrayerData` or the real tomorrow/rollover caller, not just a replacement validator. Capture all assignments to today/tomorrow, effective timezone, cache writes, error output and request count. Preserve an independent process/VM timeout around the historical Infinity RED; never inject it into the owner's live document.

| Stimulus | Required repaired result and discriminating control |
|---|---|
| Replace timings with `{}`; delete Fajr; set Dhuhr to `1e999:00` or `25:99` | Rejected before any state/cache/zone adoption; terminates; no NaN/Infinity output. Original source admission/Infinity loop must make the fixture fail. |
| Change Gregorian date and primitives to September 6 for request September 7 | Rejected, not relabeled current or silently persisted under September 7. The unchanged September 7 control loads. |
| Set timezone `Invalid/Zone`; return HTTP 500 with `{code:500,status:"ERROR",data:record}` | No timezone adoption or schedule commit. Ordinary 400 without timings remains rejected. |
| Seed the exact corrupt cache above; make fetch healthy | Cache miss, then healthy network request and usable today. Assert positive request count and persisted valid record; merely catching the error is insufficient. |
| Cache valid fixture, then deny network and storage writes | Existing valid record remains usable; write failure does not blank it. Cache namespace is unchanged. |
| Omit Hijri; set malformed optional day/month; set `month.en=7` | Times remain usable where required Gregorian identity is intact; optional date is unavailable, never NaN/00/undefined or a thrown `.slice`. |
| Use suffix clock `05:00 (UTC)`; use equal polar-like timings | Accepted clocks and finite model/arc output. Replay both complete captured polar envelopes below before claiming the bounded captured-provider compatibility; synthetic equality alone is insufficient. |
| Load isolated fallback with `config.js` unavailable and `datefmt=constructor` / `__proto__` | String literal or explicitly unavailable output; no TypeError. Repeat ordinary aliases and the three historically non-reproducing names; normal config loads retain their previous behavior. |

Use a temporary isolated mutation that removes a required-clock check, the cache guard, or the own-key guard one at a time; each corresponding fixture must fail. Restore the authorized final tree before acceptance. The mutation is a test of discrimination, not a source change to publish.

## Complete captured polar compatibility inputs

These two complete response envelopes were captured during the original provider lane, not generated from the ordinary synthetic fixture above and not fetched again for this work order. Reproduce acceptance offline from the public JSON below. The request locators describe historical provenance; a new live response is not a substitute for these bound inputs. Their Hijri source fields are preserved as provider data, not certified religious-calendar truth.

For each record, configure latitude 69.6492, longitude 18.9553, method 3, school 0 and Europe/Oslo before the real loader executes. Intercept its matching dated request with `ok:true`, HTTP 200 and the entire envelope; then exercise the actual admission, cache and `model()`/`drawArc()` consumers. Freeze local noon on the response's Gregorian day: summer 2026-06-21T10:00:00.000Z, winter 2026-12-21T11:00:00.000Z. For a cache control, store `{date: envelope.data.date.gregorian.date, data: envelope.data}` in the selected main-format key and deny network. These are proposed repaired-tree replays; the original evidence proved finite source-model/arc behavior, not new browser/repair PASS.

**tromso-summer** — original retrieval `2026-09-07T21:21:07.470Z`, HTTP 200; request `https://api.aladhan.com/v1/timings/21-06-2026?latitude=69.6492&longitude=18.9553&method=3&school=0`. SHA256 of the exact UTF-8 response text below, excluding Markdown fences and their line terminators: `1a0ef89fa1a68cb0ccdd29f3ceb1a8bafed32dc45c5a2bb8430feaad7d6fe1c4`.

```json
{"code":200,"status":"OK","data":{"timings":{"Fajr":"00:46","Sunrise":"00:46","Dhuhr":"12:46","Asr":"17:58","Sunset":"00:46","Maghrib":"00:46","Isha":"00:46","Imsak":"00:36","Midnight":"12:46","Firstthird":"08:46","Lastthird":"16:46"},"date":{"readable":"21 Jun 2026","timestamp":"1782018000","hijri":{"date":"06-01-1448","format":"DD-MM-YYYY","day":"6","weekday":{"en":"Al Ahad","ar":"الاحد"},"month":{"number":1,"en":"Muḥarram","ar":"مُحَرَّم","days":29},"year":"1448","designation":{"abbreviated":"AH","expanded":"Anno Hegirae"},"holidays":[],"adjustedHolidays":[],"method":"HJCoSA"},"gregorian":{"date":"21-06-2026","format":"DD-MM-YYYY","day":"21","weekday":{"en":"Sunday"},"month":{"number":6,"en":"June"},"year":"2026","designation":{"abbreviated":"AD","expanded":"Anno Domini"},"lunarSighting":false}},"meta":{"latitude":69.6492,"longitude":18.9553,"timezone":"Europe/Oslo","method":{"id":3,"name":"Muslim World League","params":{"Fajr":18,"Isha":17},"location":{"latitude":51.5194682,"longitude":-0.1360365}},"latitudeAdjustmentMethod":"ANGLE_BASED","midnightMode":"STANDARD","school":"STANDARD","offset":{"Imsak":0,"Fajr":0,"Sunrise":0,"Dhuhr":0,"Asr":0,"Maghrib":0,"Sunset":0,"Isha":0,"Midnight":0}}}}
```

**tromso-winter** — original retrieval `2026-09-07T21:21:07.517Z`, HTTP 200; request `https://api.aladhan.com/v1/timings/21-12-2026?latitude=69.6492&longitude=18.9553&method=3&school=0`. SHA256 of the exact UTF-8 response text below, excluding Markdown fences and their line terminators: `b7a56f538c5b306b4c7ba8e8e447870e607311c58815365563c5cc14198b2a5c`.

```json
{"code":200,"status":"OK","data":{"timings":{"Fajr":"06:28","Sunrise":"11:42","Dhuhr":"11:42","Asr":"12:14","Sunset":"11:42","Maghrib":"11:42","Isha":"16:44","Imsak":"06:18","Midnight":"23:42","Firstthird":"19:42","Lastthird":"03:42"},"date":{"readable":"21 Dec 2026","timestamp":"1797832800","hijri":{"date":"12-07-1448","format":"DD-MM-YYYY","day":"12","weekday":{"en":"Al Athnayn","ar":"الاثنين"},"month":{"number":7,"en":"Rajab","ar":"رَجَب","days":30},"year":"1448","designation":{"abbreviated":"AH","expanded":"Anno Hegirae"},"holidays":[],"adjustedHolidays":[],"method":"HJCoSA"},"gregorian":{"date":"21-12-2026","format":"DD-MM-YYYY","day":"21","weekday":{"en":"Monday"},"month":{"number":12,"en":"December"},"year":"2026","designation":{"abbreviated":"AD","expanded":"Anno Domini"},"lunarSighting":false}},"meta":{"latitude":69.6492,"longitude":18.9553,"timezone":"Europe/Oslo","method":{"id":3,"name":"Muslim World League","params":{"Fajr":18,"Isha":17},"location":{"latitude":51.5194682,"longitude":-0.1360365}},"latitudeAdjustmentMethod":"ANGLE_BASED","midnightMode":"STANDARD","school":"STANDARD","offset":{"Imsak":0,"Fajr":0,"Sunrise":0,"Dhuhr":0,"Asr":0,"Maghrib":0,"Sunset":0,"Isha":0,"Midnight":0}}}}
```

Summer has five equal 00:46 events; winter has Sunrise, Dhuhr, Sunset and Maghrib all 11:42, with Asr 12:14. Both must remain admitted with finite model and arc outputs. Do not impose increasing-order, unique-event or sunrise-before-Dhuhr rules that reject either captured schedule. The no-hang bound still applies if an input is deliberately changed to a malformed/nonfinite clock. Restore each unchanged envelope as a positive control after every rejecting mutant. A synthetically equal schedule is useful as an extra small control, but does not replace these captured records in the closure gate.

[R000A](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/10) uses the same summer timing/method record to qualify marker classification; this owner qualifies data admission and finite consumers. Keep one test fixture definition when integrated, with separate assertions for those distinct invariants. No new dependency or provider-policy repair is implied. Both complete inputs are public here; the original capture archive is optional provenance.

## Delivery, rollback and closure

The public effect is trustworthy usable prayer state and recoverable invalid input. Add the discriminating fixtures to the existing test owner; a private probe invocation alone is insufficient. Keep `index.html` self-contained. README needs only the resulting unavailable/recovery behavior. No builder field, preset version, installer change, dependency, calendar engine or cache purge follows from this issue. Admission is not output encoding; [R0001](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/1) still owns inert rendering.

Final acceptance needs the final-tree invalid/valid/cache controls, actual browser loading→error/recovery and date crops, and no regression in readable fixed 325×530 card, moon opacity or motion. Independent exact-tree review must inspect every reachable ingress and reject a validator with no callers. Record evidence before manually closing #2, with exact commit/fixture identity and limits; use non-closing `Implements #2` PR wording. A public repair claim additionally needs served-source and consumer readback; otherwise report not deployed.

If valid suffix or captured polar data is rejected, stop and narrow the grammar with evidence before widening it. Revert the coordinated admission/caller changes if rollback is needed, retaining old cache bytes and the failing fixture. Missing browser or captured-provider qualification is a named partial state, not DONE. Supplementary provenance: finding companion SHA256 `526a516cd768627ee9833e2121e48b683d16f67ac15236832b0585e0d9bc0136`; the decisive inputs above are public and do not require that private file.

title: R0001: Keep untrusted date text inert at every calendar output sink
body:
<!-- salah-widget-audit-20260907:SW-001 -->
# R0001: Keep untrusted date text inert at every calendar output sink

**Repository-local identity:** `R0001` in `theislampill/salah_widget`; existing tracker [#1](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/issues/1). The SW identifier is historical draft provenance.


The delivered-source baseline treats formatted calendar data as HTML. A crafted `datefmt` fragment reached both footer rows and ran a harmless event handler in a local browser. Repair the three date interpolations and prove that each real sink is protected. The candidate already contains a narrow encoding repair, but its helper-only smoke can remain green after a sink loses that repair.

Campaign draft alias: SW-001. Existing GitHub owner: #1. Priority P1; product defect with its directly associated regression guard. Filing or publishing this work order does not authorize implementation or certify a repair.

## Re-anchor the exact owner

Historical main is `fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624`; candidate is `9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb`. Before a future authorized change, run these read-only commands in the intended checkout and record the output:

```text
git rev-parse --show-toplevel
git remote get-url origin
git status --short
git rev-parse HEAD
git diff fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624 -- index.html config.js tests/smoke.html
```

Expected repository is `theislampill/salah_widget`. Reconcile relevant changes rather than asserting that an arbitrary future HEAD is vulnerable. Preserve unrelated dirty work. The source owners are [main formatter and render sinks, lines 687–692 and 2003–2016](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/index.html#L687), [candidate escaping and sinks](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/index.html#L694), [configuration ingress](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/fd2972ba64225fe9d6848e92497e6d0ed20ea624/config.js#L50), and [candidate security smoke, lines 220–234](https://github.com/theislampill/salah_widget/blob/9d9c43649748555afbe09e3ca49bc47db2d7e7bb/tests/smoke.html#L220).

## Incident, mechanism and evidence limits

`SalahConfig.resolve(location.hash).cfg.datefmt` supplies `datefmtStr`. `fmtDate()` substitutes documented tokens while preserving other literal characters. Main then interpolates its result into `#ce.innerHTML` and `#ah.innerHTML`. A separate pre-Maghrib preview interpolates `tomorrow.date.hijri.day` directly. API/cache month text reaches the formatter too. The missing contract is at the HTML boundary: values intentionally allowed as text must not become nodes or event attributes.

The recorded canary was exactly:

```html
<svg onload="window.__sw_sec_probe=1"></svg>
```

Historical browser route: local main `index.html` with `#lat=24.47&lon=39.61&label=Madinah&method=4&tz=Asia%2FRiyadh&simTime=12:30&simWx=0&datefmt=%3Csvg%20onload%3D%22window.__sw_sec_probe%3D1%22%3E%3C%2Fsvg%3E`. After prayer data loaded, `window.__sw_sec_probe` was `1` and the two calendar rows contained two injected SVG nodes. The equivalent candidate route recorded no canary value and zero SVG nodes. This establishes an actual local browser execution path; it does not establish exfiltration, a public-origin exploit run, or general candidate security.

Separately, exact-source replay through the real config module and recording DOM stubs tested normal, hash, provider-month and preview-day cases. Main emitted raw SVG in all three hostile cases; candidate escaped it. Those upstream cases were source execution, not browser event execution. An in-memory CE-only mutant removed `${escHtml(fmtDate(g))}` while leaving `escHtml()` intact: the old helper assertion still returned true, the benign page still contained no injected element, and the hostile hash again reached CE as raw SVG. This is why a direct helper test is insufficient.

## Smallest executable repair

1. Keep `fmtDate()` a plain-text formatter. Apply the candidate's `escHtml()` at the final CE formatted value, AH selected formatted value, and tomorrow-day preview value, or construct text nodes at those same boundaries. For the existing template structure, the narrow three-call encoding change is the preferred starting patch. Escape dynamic text once at its output context; retain constant era, phase and stale spans as markup.
2. Keep hash/config serialization literal. Do not strip angle brackets, Arabic, quotes or ampersands at ingestion; such an allowlist changes supported custom formats and still fails to cover trusted-looking provider/cache data. Do not encode in `fmtDate()` and again at the sink: double encoding would show `&` to the user and contaminate other plain-text consumers.
3. Put hostile inputs into the existing smoke owner through an isolated deterministic page load. Wire tests to the actual configuration path and renderer, not a second miniature renderer.
